name: ZITLAS Sattu Power Shot
description: A 2-minute Bihar-inspired no-cook drink-meal made by whisking roasted gram flour into water with lemon and spices — built for a hostel room with zero cooking equipment.
instructions: Add sattu to a glass or bottle.
Pour in water and whisk hard with a spoon or fork until no lumps remain.
Stir in lemon juice, roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Drink immediately — sattu settles if left standing.
why_it_works: High protein with zero cooking
Works with just a bottle and spoon
Very low cost

name: ZITLAS Moong Cheela Paneer Roll
description: A savoury moong dal crepe rolled around a lightly spiced paneer-spinach filling — a complete protein breakfast eaten like a wrap.
ingredients: Moong dal (soaked, ground to batter) — 50 g
instructions: Grind soaked moong dal with ginger-chilli paste and a little water into a smooth, pourable batter.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a thin crepe. Cook 2 minutes until set.
Meanwhile, saute onion in oil with cumin seeds, then add paneer and spinach; cook 3-4 minutes.
Place the filling along one edge of the cheela and roll it up tightly.
Slice in half and serve warm.
why_it_works: Two complementary protein sources in one wrap
Naturally gluten-free
Portable once rolled

name: ZITLAS Leftover Rice Protein Poha
description: Turns yesterday's plain cooked rice into a soft, savoury breakfast by pan-tossing it poha-style with peanuts, moong sprouts and turmeric — no fresh grain needed.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Heat oil in a kadai, add mustard seeds and let them splutter, then add curry leaves and peanuts, roast lightly.
Add onion and saute until translucent.
Add moong sprouts and cook 2-3 minutes.
Add cold leftover rice and turmeric, breaking up any clumps, and toss on medium heat for 3-4 minutes until heated through.
Serve hot with a squeeze of lemon.
why_it_works: Prevents food waste from last night's rice
Sprouts add fresh crunch and protein
Ready in under 15 minutes

name: ZITLAS Egg Bhurji Paratha Roll
description: Spiced scrambled egg wrapped inside a whole wheat paratha, cut into a lunchbox-ready roll for the commute to office or college.
instructions: Knead the atta into a firm dough with water and roll out into a roti; roast on a dry tawa until lightly done.
In the same tawa, heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft.
Beat the egg and pour in, scramble with turmeric and chilli powder until fully cooked.
Spread the bhurji along the roti and roll it up tightly.
Wrap in foil or paper for carrying.
why_it_works: Complete protein wrapped for easy carrying
Uses one pan for both roti and filling
Good pre-commute breakfast

name: ZITLAS Overnight Chia Peanut Jar
description: Chia seeds and oats soaked overnight in milk with peanut butter and banana — no cooking required, ready to grab straight from the fridge.
instructions: Combine chia seeds, oats and milk in a jar, stir well to prevent clumping.
Add peanut butter and mix through.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight (minimum 6 hours).
Top with sliced banana just before eating.
why_it_works: Zero morning cooking time
High fiber from chia and oats
Can be prepped for 3-4 days at once

name: ZITLAS Kettle Oats with Roasted Chana
description: Rolled oats cooked using only boiling water from an electric kettle, finished with roasted chana and milk powder for crunch and protein — built for hostel rooms with no stove.
instructions: Boil water in the electric kettle.
Add oats and milk powder to a mug, pour in the boiling water, stir and cover for 3-4 minutes.
Stir in roasted chana for crunch.
Season with salt for a savoury version or a little jaggery for sweet, and eat straight from the mug.
why_it_works: Needs only a kettle and a mug
Roasted chana adds protein and crunch without cooking
Very low cost

name: ZITLAS Besan Dhokla Bites
description: Steamed gram-flour dhokla made in an idli mould, giving the classic Gujarati texture without deep steamer equipment.
ingredients: Eno fruit salt / baking soda — 3 g
instructions: Whisk besan, curd and water into a smooth, thick-pourable batter.
Just before steaming, mix in the fruit salt/baking soda — it will froth slightly.
Pour into a greased idli mould or shallow tin and steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 12-15 minutes.
Cool slightly, cut into squares.
Temper oil with mustard and sesame seeds and pour over the top.
why_it_works: Steamed, not fried — very low added fat
Uses standard home pressure cooker as a steamer
Good fiber from besan

name: ZITLAS No-Cook Sprouted Moong Chaat
description: A tangy, crunchy sprouted moong salad with onion, tomato and lemon — ready in five minutes with no heat at all.
instructions: Rinse the sprouts well.
Toss sprouts with onion, tomato and coriander in a bowl.
Add lemon juice and chaat masala.
Mix well and eat immediately for maximum crunch.
why_it_works: Zero cooking, zero cleanup beyond one bowl
High fiber and protein together
Very low calorie for weight-loss mornings

name: ZITLAS Bajra Khichdi Bowl
description: A pressure-cooker millet-and-moong khichdi that makes a warm, fibre-rich family breakfast bowl, especially suited to cooler mornings.
instructions: Rinse moong dal; combine with bajra flour, vegetables, turmeric and enough water in the cooker.
Pressure cook for 3-4 whistles until soft and porridge-like.
Once pressure releases, mash lightly for a smoother texture.
Temper ghee with cumin seeds and pour over the top before serving.
why_it_works: High-fibre millet base is unusual outside dinner khichdi
Good for cold mornings and shared family portions
Naturally gluten-free

name: ZITLAS Curd Rice with Roasted Peanuts
description: A cooling South Indian-style curd rice tempered with mustard, curry leaves and roasted peanuts — light, quick, and needs almost no active cooking.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chilli — 3 g
instructions: Mash the cold rice slightly and mix with curd and a splash of milk to loosen it.
In a small kadai, heat oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chilli and peanuts; roast until peanuts are golden.
Pour the tempering over the curd rice and mix.
Serve at room temperature or lightly chilled.
why_it_works: Very light on the stomach for hot mornings
Minimal cooking, mostly assembly
Good gut-friendly probiotic base

name: ZITLAS Soya Keema Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha where the filling is spiced, finely crumbled soya granules instead of meat keema — a vegetarian high-protein take on a keema paratha.
instructions: Saute onion, tomato, ginger-garlic paste and garam masala with soya granules until dry and well spiced; cool slightly.
Knead atta into a dough; roll a portion, place the soya filling in the centre, fold and seal.
Roll out gently into a thick paratha.
Roast on a tawa with a little oil on both sides until golden with brown spots.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Soya keema has more protein per gram than most meat keema
Filling doubles as a standalone snack too
Satisfying, higher-effort weekend breakfast

name: ZITLAS Peanut Banana Oats Smoothie Bowl
description: A thick, spoonable oats-and-banana smoothie topped with peanuts — a cold breakfast bowl for hot mornings, made entirely in a mixer.
instructions: Blend oats, banana, milk and curd together until thick and smooth.
Pour into a bowl — it should be thick enough to eat with a spoon, not sip.
Top with crushed peanuts and a few banana slices.
Eat immediately for best texture.
why_it_works: No heat needed, good for summer mornings
Banana adds natural sweetness without added sugar
Peanuts add crunch and healthy fat

name: ZITLAS Egg White Veggie Wrap
description: A lean egg-white omelette loaded with vegetables and rolled into a whole wheat wrap — designed for lower fat intake while keeping protein high.
instructions: Roll the atta into a thin roti and dry-roast it lightly; set aside.
Whisk egg whites with black pepper.
Heat oil in a pan, saute capsicum and onion for 2 minutes, then pour in egg whites and cook until just set, not rubbery.
Place the egg-white filling onto the roti and roll tightly.
Slice and serve.
why_it_works: Very low fat, high protein combination
Vegetables add volume and fiber without many calories
Good for a lean cutting phase

name: ZITLAS Rajma Paratha (Leftover Rescue)
description: Leftover cooked rajma is mashed and spiced to become a paratha stuffing, turning last night's dinner curry into a fresh breakfast.
instructions: Drain excess gravy from the leftover rajma and mash the beans coarsely with onion, ajwain and chilli powder.
Knead the atta into a dough; stuff a portion with the rajma mixture and seal.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Serve with curd or pickle.
why_it_works: Directly repurposes last night's leftovers instead of discarding them
Rajma brings both protein and fiber
No separate filling has to be cooked from scratch

name: ZITLAS Ragi Dosa with Tomato Chutney
description: A fibre-forward finger-millet dosa batter pan-cooked thin and crisp, served with a quick tomato chutney — a fiber-focused twist on a South Indian classic.
instructions: Whisk ragi flour, rice flour and curd with water into a thin, pourable batter; rest 15 minutes.
For chutney, blend tomato with green chilli and a pinch of salt, then temper with cumin seeds in a little oil.
Heat a tawa, pour batter in a circular motion from the edge inward to form a thin dosa.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until crisp; flip briefly.
Serve hot with the tomato chutney.
why_it_works: Ragi has notably more fiber and calcium than a plain rice dosa
No fermentation wait required
Naturally gluten-free

name: ZITLAS Sattu Paratha
description: A Bihar-style stuffed paratha filled with a spiced sattu mixture — a budget protein breakfast that also travels well for lunch.
instructions: Mix sattu with chopped onion, ajwain, pickle masala and a little water into a thick, moist stuffing.
Knead the atta into a dough, stuff with the sattu mixture and seal well.
Roll out carefully and roast on a tawa with mustard oil until well browned on both sides.
Serve hot with curd or pickle.
why_it_works: Sattu is one of the cheapest high-protein ingredients available in India
Filling stays moist without any dairy needed
Travels well for lunchboxes too

name: ZITLAS Makhana Yogurt Parfait
description: Layered Greek yogurt and roasted fox nuts (makhana) with a touch of honey — a light, crunchy breakfast that eats almost like a dessert.
instructions: Spoon a layer of Greek yogurt into a glass.
Sprinkle a layer of crushed roasted makhana over it.
Repeat the layers once more.
Drizzle honey on top just before serving to keep the makhana crunchy.
why_it_works: High protein-to-calorie ratio from Greek yogurt
Makhana adds crunch with very little fat
Zero cooking involved

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Dalia Upma
description: Broken wheat cooked upma-style with vegetables in a pressure cooker — a fibre-dense, family-portioned alternative to rava upma.
instructions: Dry-roast the dalia lightly until aromatic; set aside.
Heat oil in the cooker, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then saute onion and vegetables for 3-4 minutes.
Add the roasted dalia and water in a 1:2.5 ratio, season with salt.
Pressure cook for 2 whistles, then let pressure release naturally before opening.
why_it_works: Notably higher fiber than a rava-based upma
Cooks unattended in a pressure cooker
Large batch suits a family breakfast

name: ZITLAS Boiled Egg Sprouts Bowl
description: A no-cook combination of boiled eggs and mixed sprouts tossed with lemon and pepper — a fast, high-protein bowl for right after a morning workout.
instructions: Chop the boiled eggs into quarters.
Toss with sprouts and onion in a bowl.
Add lemon juice and black pepper.
Mix gently and eat immediately after your workout.
why_it_works: Fast-digesting protein combination suited for post-workout timing
Requires only a boiled egg made ahead — no stove needed at breakfast time
High protein for the calorie cost

name: ZITLAS Besan Savoury Toast
description: Whole wheat bread dipped in a spiced besan batter and pan-toasted, like a savoury French toast — a five-minute upgrade on plain toast.
instructions: Whisk besan with water, onion, turmeric and ajwain into a thick, spreadable batter.
Dip each bread slice into the batter, coating both sides.
Pan-toast on a lightly oiled tawa until golden on both sides.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Adds meaningful protein and fiber to an otherwise low-protein breakfast staple
Only one pan and five minutes of cooking
Cheaper than most spreads or jams

name: ZITLAS Thecha Peanut Sandwich
description: A Maharashtrian-style spicy peanut-garlic thecha spread inside a grilled whole wheat sandwich — a quick, bold-flavoured budget breakfast.
instructions: Dry-roast peanuts, then pound or blend coarsely with garlic and green chilli into a thick thecha paste.
Spread the thecha between two bread slices.
Grill on a lightly oiled tawa until both sides are golden and crisp.
Cut and serve hot.
why_it_works: Peanut base gives more protein and healthy fat than butter or jam
Very budget-friendly, no dairy required
Distinct regional flavour instead of a generic sandwich

name: ZITLAS Protein-Boosted Idli Sambar
description: Regular idli batter enriched with extra soaked urad and moong dal before steaming, served with a protein-added sambar using extra toor dal.
ingredients: Extra moong dal, soaked and blended in — 30 g
instructions: Blend the extra soaked moong dal into the fermented idli batter just before steaming, mixing gently to keep it airy.
Steam the batter in idli moulds for 10-12 minutes until a knife comes out clean.
Separately pressure cook toor dal with vegetables until soft, then simmer with sambar powder and tamarind to make the sambar.
Serve idlis hot with the sambar.
why_it_works: Extra dal in the batter raises protein without changing the familiar taste
Sambar itself becomes a second protein source, not just a side
Steamed, not fried

name: ZITLAS Paneer Roti Roll (Lunchbox)
description: Leftover roti spread with a mashed spiced paneer filling and rolled up — designed specifically to be packed and eaten a few hours later.
instructions: Warm the leftover roti lightly on a tawa so it stays pliable.
Mash paneer with onion, chaat masala and a little oil into a coarse filling.
Spread the filling along the roti and roll tightly.
Wrap in foil — it holds together well for 3-4 hours without going soggy.
why_it_works: Repurposes leftover roti instead of making fresh dough
Stays intact for a mid-morning lunchbox eat
Higher protein than a typical roti roll

name: ZITLAS Soya Brown Rice Prep Bowl
description: A make-ahead bowl of spiced soya chunks over brown rice, portioned into containers for grab-and-go mornings across the week.
instructions: Cook brown rice separately and let it cool fully before portioning (this keeps it from going mushy in storage).
Heat oil, saute onion and ginger-garlic paste, add vegetables and cook 4-5 minutes.
Add rehydrated soya chunks and garam masala, cook until well coated and slightly dry, about 8-10 minutes.
Divide brown rice and the soya mixture into 4 containers.
Refrigerate; reheat one portion each morning for up to 4 days.
why_it_works: One cooking session covers 4 mornings
Soya chunks are one of the highest-protein-per-rupee options available
Brown rice adds fiber compared to white rice

name: ZITLAS Peanut Sprouts Kanda Poha
description: Classic Maharashtrian kanda poha with peanuts, upgraded by folding in moong sprouts at the end for extra crunch and protein.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Rinse poha in a sieve under running water until softened; do not soak.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then add peanuts and roast lightly.
Add onion and saute until translucent.
Add turmeric and the rinsed poha, mix gently on low heat for 2-3 minutes.
Fold in the moong sprouts at the very end so they stay crunchy, and serve immediately.
why_it_works: Sprouts added at the end keep their crunch and boost protein over standard poha
Still recognisably the familiar dish, just meaningfully upgraded
Very quick and low cost

name: ZITLAS Egg Akuri on Toast
description: A Parsi-style softly spiced scrambled egg with ginger, chilli and coriander, served over toasted whole wheat bread.
instructions: Toast the bread slices until lightly crisp.
Heat oil, saute onion, ginger and green chilli until soft, then add tomato and cook until pulpy.
Beat the eggs and pour in; stir continuously on low heat for a soft, slightly wet scramble rather than dry.
Finish with chopped coriander and spoon over the toast.
why_it_works: Slow, low-heat scrambling keeps the egg tender rather than rubbery
A distinct regional variation on the usual bhurji
Balanced protein-to-carb ratio with the toast

name: ZITLAS Oats Idli
description: Ground rolled oats combined with urad dal batter and steamed like a regular idli — a fibre-forward variation for people who don't enjoy oats as porridge.
instructions: Grind rolled oats to a coarse flour and mix with the fermented urad dal batter and curd.
Rest the mixed batter for 10 minutes.
Add eno fruit salt just before steaming and mix gently.
Pour into greased idli moulds and steam for 10-12 minutes in a pressure cooker without the whistle.
why_it_works: Delivers oats' fiber benefit in a texture many people prefer over porridge
Steamed preparation stays low in added fat
Works well for people who dislike oats' usual mushy texture

name: ZITLAS Air-Fried Moong Dahi Vada
description: Mini moong dal vadas air-fried instead of deep-fried, soaked briefly in curd — a protein-forward, lower-oil take on dahi vada for breakfast.
instructions: Grind the soaked moong dal with ginger and green chilli into a thick batter; do not add water.
Shape into small discs and brush lightly with oil.
Air fry at 180°C for 12-15 minutes, flipping once, until golden.
Soak the air-fried vadas in whisked curd for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle roasted cumin powder and serve.
why_it_works: Air frying cuts most of the oil a normal fried vada would use
Moong dal delivers more protein than the usual urad-based vada
Curd adds a second protein layer

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Omelette Roll
description: A whole-egg omelette loaded with vegetables, rolled up like a wrap without any bread — a quick, low-carb office breakfast.
instructions: Beat the eggs with black pepper.
Heat oil in a flat pan, saute the vegetables for 2 minutes.
Pour the beaten egg evenly over the vegetables and cook on low-medium heat until just set.
Roll the omelette up from one side using a spatula.
Slice in half and serve.
why_it_works: No bread keeps carbs low while protein stays high
Cooked and rolled entirely in one pan
Ready in well under 15 minutes

name: ZITLAS Chana Dal Vegetable Cheela
description: A savoury chana dal batter crepe packed with grated vegetables — a fibre-and-protein alternative to a plain besan chilla.
ingredients: Chana dal, soaked and ground — 70 g
instructions: Grind the soaked chana dal with green chilli into a smooth, pourable batter.
Mix in the grated carrot and cabbage along with cumin seeds.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a thick cheela.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Chana dal has more fiber per gram than besan
Vegetables are mixed into the batter, not just a side garnish
Naturally gluten-free

name: ZITLAS No-Bake Peanut Chikki Bites
description: Small no-bake energy bites made from roasted peanuts and jaggery, portioned for a grab-and-go breakfast when there's genuinely no time to sit down.
instructions: Melt jaggery with ghee in a kadai on low heat until it forms a thick syrup.
Turn off the heat and quickly mix in the crushed peanuts, coating them evenly.
While still warm, shape into 8 small bite-sized balls.
Cool completely, then store in an airtight container for up to a week; grab 2 on your way out.
why_it_works: Genuinely eat-on-the-move — no bowl or spoon needed
Batch-made once, lasts most of a week
Uses jaggery instead of refined sugar

name: ZITLAS Bajra Roti with Peanut Chutney
description: A Rajasthani-style millet flatbread served with a dry roasted peanut chutney and a side of curd — a hearty, fibre-rich regional breakfast.
instructions: Knead bajra flour with warm water into a dough (it's less elastic than wheat, so pat it out by hand rather than rolling).
Cook the flattened roti on a hot tawa until browned on both sides, brushing with a little ghee.
For the chutney, dry-roast peanuts and pound coarsely with garlic, red chilli and salt.
Serve the roti hot with the peanut chutney and a bowl of curd on the side.
why_it_works: Bajra has more fiber and minerals than wheat
Peanut chutney adds protein without any dairy dependence
Traditional combination that's naturally balanced

name: ZITLAS Soya Milk Date Overnight Oats
description: A vegan overnight oats jar made with soya milk and chopped dates instead of honey — sweetened naturally and higher in plant protein.
instructions: Combine oats, soya milk, chopped dates and chia seeds in a jar.
Stir well so the chia doesn't clump.
Seal and refrigerate overnight.
Stir again before eating in the morning.
why_it_works: Fully vegan protein sources instead of dairy
Dates provide natural sweetness with fiber attached
Zero morning prep time

name: ZITLAS Lite Paneer Paratha
description: A stuffed paneer paratha made with a deliberately reduced-oil roasting method, keeping the classic flavour with meaningfully less added fat.
instructions: Mix paneer with onion, ajwain and garam masala; no oil needed in the filling itself.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the paneer mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a hot tawa using only a light brushing of oil rather than pooling oil, flipping to get even colour.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Uses a fraction of the oil a typical paratha uses while keeping the texture
Paneer keeps protein high even with less fat overall
Still recognisably the familiar comfort food

name: ZITLAS Soya Vermicelli Upma
description: Roasted vermicelli upma with soya granules folded in — a South Indian breakfast staple made noticeably more filling.
instructions: Dry-roast the vermicelli until light golden; set aside.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then saute onion and carrot for 3 minutes.
Add the rehydrated soya granules and cook 2 minutes.
Add the roasted vermicelli with hot water (roughly equal volume) and cook covered until the water is absorbed.
why_it_works: Soya granules meaningfully raise the protein of a usually low-protein dish
Still cooks in one pan in under 20 minutes
Familiar taste, upgraded composition

name: ZITLAS Chana Curd Bhel (No Cook)
description: Boiled chana tossed with curd, onion and tomato in a bhel-style mix — tangy, filling, and entirely no-cook.
instructions: Combine boiled chana, onion and tomato in a bowl.
Add curd and chaat masala, mix well.
Top with chopped coriander.
Eat immediately while the onion is still crisp.
why_it_works: Two protein sources combined with zero cooking
Curd makes it noticeably lighter than an oil-based chaat
Ready in under 10 minutes

name: ZITLAS Baked Egg Muffin Cups
description: Whisked eggs and chopped vegetables baked in a muffin tin into individual portions — a genuine meal-prep breakfast for the whole week.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C and lightly grease a 6-cavity muffin tin.
Whisk all the eggs together with salt and pepper.
Divide the chopped vegetables evenly among the muffin cups, then pour whisked egg over each.
Bake for 18-20 minutes until set and lightly domed.
Cool, then refrigerate; microwave one or two cups each morning for up to 4 days.
why_it_works: Six single-serve portions from one batch cooking session
Reheats in under a minute on busy mornings
Vegetables are baked in, not garnished after

name: ZITLAS Sabudana Peanut Khichdi
description: A protein-supported version of Maharashtrian sabudana khichdi, with a larger peanut ratio and a side of curd to balance out the starch-heavy sago base. Note: sabudana needs 4+ hours of prior soaking, not counted in active prep time below.
instructions: Soak sabudana in just enough water to cover it, for at least 4 hours or overnight, until pearls are soft but separate.
Heat oil, temper cumin seeds and green chilli, then saute diced potato until soft.
Add the soaked sabudana and crushed peanuts, tossing gently on low heat until translucent, about 6-8 minutes.
Serve hot with a side of curd for extra protein.
why_it_works: Deliberately peanut-heavy ratio compensates for sabudana's low protein
Curd on the side adds a second protein source
Traditional fasting-day dish made more nutritionally complete

name: ZITLAS Multigrain Uttapam
description: A thick, vegetable-topped pancake made from a multigrain batter (rice, urad and a portion of oats) — a heartier alternative to a plain dosa.
ingredients: Oats, ground and mixed in — 30 g
instructions: Mix ground oats into the fermented dosa batter and rest for 10 minutes.
Heat a tawa, pour a thick ladle of batter and spread only slightly (uttapam stays thick, unlike dosa).
Scatter onion and tomato over the top and press gently.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until the base is golden, then flip briefly.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Thicker format holds more toppings than a thin dosa
Oats addition adds fiber to a usually rice-heavy batter
Vegetables are cooked into the surface, not a side dish

name: ZITLAS Leftover Roti Chivda
description: Stale leftover rotis are torn into pieces and pan-toasted with peanuts and spices into a crunchy, chivda-style snack-breakfast — genuinely rescues rotis that would otherwise be thrown out.
ingredients: Leftover roti, torn into small pieces — 100 g
Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Heat oil in a kadai, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then roast the peanuts until golden.
Add onion and saute until soft.
Add the torn roti pieces and turmeric, tossing continuously on medium-high heat until the pieces crisp up slightly, about 5 minutes.
Serve hot as-is — it eats like a savoury chivda.
why_it_works: Rescues rotis heading for the bin rather than being reheated plain
Crisping the roti gives it a completely different texture from a reheated roti
Very low cost since the base ingredient is already leftover

name: ZITLAS One-Pan Hostel Paneer Chilla Wrap
description: A besan-paneer batter cooked directly as a folded wrap in a single pan — designed for a hostel room with just an induction plate and one pan.
instructions: Whisk besan with water, turmeric and chilli powder into a smooth batter.
Stir the crumbled paneer and onion directly into the batter.
Heat the single pan on the induction plate with a little oil, pour the batter in and spread into a thick round.
Cook 2-3 minutes until the base sets, flip, and cook the other side.
Fold in half like a wrap and eat straight from the pan.
why_it_works: Everything — batter, protein and cooking — happens in one pan
No separate filling step, unlike a stuffed paratha
Realistic for genuine one-induction-one-pan hostel setups

name: ZITLAS Portion-Controlled Moong Dal Halwa
description: A small, deliberately portion-capped serving of moong dal halwa made with less ghee than the traditional version — a controlled way to have a classic sweet at breakfast.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and coarsely ground — 40 g
instructions: Heat ghee in a kadai and roast the ground moong dal on low heat until it turns golden and aromatic, about 8 minutes.
Add milk gradually, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Once thickened, add jaggery and cardamom powder, stirring until it melts in and the mixture pulls together.
Serve warm in a small bowl — this recipe is intentionally single-serving to keep the portion controlled.
why_it_works: Single-serving format prevents the usual over-serving of a rich halwa
Meaningfully less ghee than a restaurant-style halwa while staying satisfying
Moong dal itself adds real protein, unusual for a dessert

name: ZITLAS Egg Oats Savoury Porridge
description: An unusual but practical combination — oats cooked savoury in stock-like water, finished with a stirred-in egg for extra protein, like a simple congee.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until soft.
Add water and bring to a simmer, then stir in the oats and cook 4-5 minutes until porridge-like.
Beat the egg lightly and stir it into the simmering oats in a thin stream, so it cooks into ribbons rather than clumping.
Season with black pepper and a dash of soy sauce, and serve hot.
why_it_works: Savoury porridge format is a genuinely different way to eat oats, not just sweetened oats again
Egg stirred in raises protein meaningfully over plain oats
One pan, under 15 minutes

name: ZITLAS Rajma Oats Tikki Sandwich
description: Leftover rajma mashed with oats as a binder, shaped into tikkis and pan-fried, then sandwiched between toasted bread — a leftover-rescue recipe with a sandwich format.
instructions: Drain excess liquid from the leftover rajma and mash it coarsely.
Mix in ground oats, onion and chilli powder — the oats bind the mixture and add fiber.
Shape into a flat tikki and pan-fry in oil until crisp on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Toast the bread lightly and sandwich the tikki inside with a spread of your choice.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Oats replace refined breadcrumbs as the binder, adding fiber instead of empty carbs
Second genuinely different way to use leftover rajma beyond the paratha version
Familiar sandwich format for people who want something handheld

name: ZITLAS Chaas and Roasted Chana Combo
description: A savoury spiced buttermilk paired with a small side of roasted chana — a light drink-plus-snack combo breakfast for very hot mornings or a light-appetite day.
ingredients: Roasted cumin powder, black salt — 3 g
instructions: Whisk the buttermilk with roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Pour into a glass.
Serve alongside a small bowl of roasted chana to eat on the side.
No cooking or cleanup beyond one glass and one bowl.
why_it_works: Very light option for mornings with a poor appetite or hot weather
Two small protein sources instead of one large meal
Genuinely no-cook and near-zero cleanup

name: ZITLAS Foxtail Millet Upma
description: Foxtail millet cooked upma-style with vegetables and peanuts — a premium-grain alternative to rava upma with a lower glycemic profile.
instructions: Rinse the foxtail millet well and soak for 10 minutes.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, roast the peanuts, then add vegetables and saute 3 minutes.
Add the soaked millet and water in a 1:2 ratio, cover and simmer for 10-12 minutes until soft.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.
why_it_works: Lower glycemic index than rava, useful for steadier morning energy
Naturally gluten-free grain option
Still cooks in one pan like a familiar upma

name: ZITLAS Paneer Bhurji Multigrain Bowl
description: Spiced scrambled paneer served over a base of mixed millets instead of bread or rice — a bowl format for people who prefer eating with a spoon.
instructions: Cook the foxtail millet ahead (or use leftover cooked millet) and keep warm.
Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add turmeric and chilli powder.
Add crumbled paneer and cook 3-4 minutes, stirring gently so it stays soft, not rubbery.
Spoon the paneer bhurji over the millet base in a bowl and serve.
why_it_works: Millet base gives more fiber than the usual bread pairing with bhurji
Bowl format suits people who find paratha or toast too heavy
High protein-to-carb ratio

name: ZITLAS Tofu Bhurji Toast
description: Crumbled tofu scrambled with Indian spices, served over toast — a fully vegan alternative to egg bhurji with a similar texture.
instructions: Toast the bread slices lightly.
Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, then add turmeric and chilli powder.
Add crumbled tofu and cook 4-5 minutes, mashing slightly for an egg-bhurji-like texture.
Spoon the tofu bhurji over the toast and serve.
why_it_works: Vegan option with a texture close enough to egg bhurji to satisfy the same craving
Tofu absorbs Indian spices well despite being a non-traditional ingredient here
Quick, one-pan filling

name: ZITLAS Quinoa Vegetable Poha-Style Bowl
description: Cooked quinoa tempered and tossed poha-style with peanuts and vegetables — for users who want a complete-protein grain instead of flattened rice.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Cook quinoa ahead of time (or use leftover cooked quinoa) and keep aside.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, roast peanuts, then saute onion and carrot for 3 minutes.
Add turmeric and the cooked quinoa, tossing gently for 3-4 minutes until heated through.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Quinoa is a rare complete-protein plant grain, unlike rice or poha
Same familiar tempering technique as regular poha, so it's easy to adapt to
Good general-fitness option though a pricier grain

name: ZITLAS Curd Sattu Cooler Bowl
description: A cold, spoonable no-cook bowl combining sattu with thick curd instead of water — heavier and more filling than the Sattu Power Shot drink, meant for a sit-down breakfast rather than a grab-and-go one.
ingredients: Roasted cumin powder, black salt — 3 g
instructions: Whisk sattu into the curd until fully smooth, with no dry lumps.
Fold in finely chopped onion.
Season with roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Top with coriander and eat with a spoon, straight from the bowl.
why_it_works: Bowl format makes it more filling than the drink version of sattu
Two protein sources — dal-based and dairy — in one no-cook dish
No equipment beyond a bowl and whisk

name: ZITLAS Masala Oats Khichdi
description: Rolled oats cooked khichdi-style with toor dal and vegetables in one pot — a savoury oats format for people who dislike sweet porridge oats.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, turmeric, curry leaves — 3 g
instructions: Rinse toor dal and pressure cook with vegetables and turmeric for 2 whistles until soft.
Dry-roast the oats separately for 2 minutes until lightly toasted.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, add the cooked dal-vegetable mix and the roasted oats with a little water.
Simmer 3-4 minutes until the oats soften into a khichdi consistency.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Savoury format avoids the usual sweet-oats fatigue
One-pot, mostly hands-off cooking
Dal brings meaningfully more protein than oats alone

name: ZITLAS Besan Paneer Roll
description: A besan crepe rolled (not folded) around a dry-spiced paneer filling — a different construction from a folded chilla, closer to a kathi roll.
instructions: Whisk besan and water into a thin, dosa-like batter.
Pan-cook a thin round on a hot tawa, similar to a dosa rather than a thick chilla.
Separately dry-toss paneer with onion and chaat masala (no extra oil needed here).
Lay the filling along one edge of the thin besan crepe and roll tightly kathi-roll style.
Slice and serve.
why_it_works: Thin-roll format is a genuinely different eating experience from a folded chilla
Dry-tossed filling keeps added fat lower
Portable once rolled

name: ZITLAS Egg Curry with Multigrain Roti
description: Boiled eggs simmered in a light onion-tomato curry, served with a multigrain roti — a curry format rather than the usual bhurji or omelette.
instructions: Knead the multigrain atta into a dough and roll into rotis; roast on a tawa and keep warm.
Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cook until pulpy.
Add garam masala and a little water to form a light gravy; simmer 5 minutes.
Halve the boiled eggs and add them into the gravy, simmering 2-3 minutes.
Serve hot with the rotis.
why_it_works: Curry format is a genuinely different way to eat eggs from bhurji or omelette
Multigrain roti adds fiber the usual white-flour roti lacks
Filling, complete meal-style breakfast

name: ZITLAS Moong Dal Tikki Sandwich
description: Boiled and mashed moong dal shaped into pan-fried tikkis and sandwiched in toasted bread — a patty-in-sandwich format distinct from a wrap or roll.
ingredients: Moong dal, boiled and mashed — 100 g
Red chilli powder, coriander powder — 3 g
instructions: Mash the boiled moong dal with onion and spices into a firm mixture.
Shape into a flat tikki.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Toast the bread and sandwich the tikki inside.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Patty format holds together better than loose dal for a sandwich
Cheap, filling, and genuinely different texture from a wrap
Good option for people who find rolls hard to eat on the move

name: ZITLAS Peanut Curd Dip with Veg Sticks
description: A thick spiced peanut-curd dip served with raw steamed vegetable sticks — an unusual dipping-format breakfast that's essentially no-cook.
instructions: Whisk curd with crushed peanuts and roasted cumin powder into a thick dip.
Cut carrot and cucumber into sticks.
Arrange the vegetable sticks around the dip.
Eat by dipping — no utensils beyond a bowl needed.
why_it_works: Genuinely no-cook, unlike most vegetable-based breakfasts
High raw-vegetable volume for very few calories
Different eating format keeps breakfast varied

name: ZITLAS Soya Frankie Roll
description: A Mumbai street-food-style frankie: spiced soya granules rolled inside a lightly charred wheat roti with onion and a tangy sauce.
instructions: Roll out the atta into a roti and roast on a tawa until slightly charred at the edges.
Separately, saute the rehydrated soya granules with pav bhaji masala until well coated and slightly dry.
Spread green and tamarind chutney on the roti, add the soya filling and sliced onion.
Roll tightly frankie-style and wrap the bottom in paper.
Serve immediately while the roti is warm.
why_it_works: Street-food frankie format is distinct from a paratha or kathi roll
Two chutneys give a genuinely different flavour profile from other rolls in the database
Good grab-and-eat option for a commute

name: ZITLAS Kuttu Pancake with Curd
description: A fasting-day-style buckwheat (kuttu) flour pancake, pan-cooked and served with plain curd — a gluten-free option using a flour rarely seen outside Navratri cooking.
instructions: Whisk kuttu flour with water, rock salt and finely chopped green chilli into a thick batter.
Heat oil on a tawa, pour the batter and spread into a small thick pancake (kuttu doesn't spread thin easily).
Cook 2-3 minutes per side until firm and lightly browned.
Serve with a side of plain curd.
why_it_works: Genuinely gluten-free flour choice, unusual outside fasting contexts
Distinct nutty flavour keeps the breakfast rotation varied
Curd on the side adds protein the flour itself lacks

name: ZITLAS Egg-Coated Paratha
description: A whole wheat paratha dipped in beaten egg and pan-cooked so the egg forms a coating on the outside, rather than being stuffed inside — an anda-paratha street-food style.
instructions: Knead atta into a dough, roll out and dry-roast a plain paratha until about 70% done.
Beat the egg with onion, pepper and chilli flakes.
Dip the half-cooked paratha into the beaten egg, coating one side.
Return to the tawa, egg-side down, with a little oil, and cook until the egg sets and browns.
Flip briefly, then serve.
why_it_works: Coating technique is genuinely different construction from a stuffed paratha
Familiar street-food format (anda paratha) most people already enjoy
One dough, one egg, one pan

name: ZITLAS Sprout Paneer Tikki
description: Mashed sprouted moong combined with crumbled paneer, shaped into pan-fried patties — a distinct patty format pairing two protein sources directly rather than as filling.
ingredients: Coriander, green chilli, cumin powder — 5 g
instructions: Coarsely grind the moong sprouts (don't puree fully — keep some texture).
Mix with crumbled paneer, onion, coriander, green chilli and cumin powder.
Shape into 3-4 small tikkis.
Pan-fry in oil until golden on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Two proteins combined directly into one patty, not one as filling for the other
Notably high protein density for the calorie cost
Good make-ahead-and-fry option

name: ZITLAS Rajgira Milk Porridge
description: Amaranth (rajgira) flour cooked into a warm milk porridge with dates — a fasting-day grain used here as a regular sweet breakfast porridge.
instructions: Whisk rajgira flour into a little cold milk first to avoid lumps.
Heat the remaining milk in a pan, add the flour mixture and stir continuously.
Simmer 6-8 minutes until thickened, stirring often.
Stir in chopped dates and cardamom powder, cook 2 more minutes, and serve warm.
why_it_works: Amaranth has a notably different mineral and fiber profile from wheat or rava porridges
Naturally gluten-free
Dates sweeten without refined sugar

name: ZITLAS Chana Sundal Bowl
description: A South Indian temple-style tempered chickpea sundal, eaten as a warm protein bowl rather than the usual evening snack serving.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, dried red chilli — 3 g
instructions: Heat oil in a kadai, temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and dried red chilli.
Add the boiled chana and toss for 3-4 minutes until well coated.
Stir in grated coconut at the end.
Serve warm as a bowl rather than a small snack portion.
why_it_works: Reframes a traditional snack as a full breakfast portion, not a trivial rename
Very low oil for the protein and fiber delivered
Quick, one-pan preparation

name: ZITLAS Moong Dal Appe
description: A moong dal and semolina batter steamed-fried into small round appe (paniyaram) using a dedicated appe pan — a distinctly different cooking format from a flat crepe.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 70 g
instructions: Mix ground moong dal with rava, onion, carrot and a little water into a thick batter; rest 10 minutes.
Heat the appe pan and add a few drops of oil into each cavity.
Pour batter into each cavity, filling about three-quarters full.
Cover and cook on low heat for 3-4 minutes, then flip each ball gently and cook the other side.
Serve hot with chutney.
why_it_works: Appe format cooks with far less oil than a pan-fried version of the same batter
Small round shape is easy for kids and makes a good family breakfast
Genuinely different mouthfeel — crisp outside, soft inside

name: ZITLAS Oats Besan Dhokla
description: A steamed dhokla batter made with ground oats mixed into besan — a fiber-boosted variation on the classic Gujarati steamed snack.
instructions: Whisk besan, ground oats, curd and water into a smooth, thick-pourable batter.
Add eno fruit salt just before steaming and mix gently until it froths slightly.
Pour into a greased tin and steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 12-15 minutes.
Cool slightly, cut into squares, and temper with mustard and sesame seeds in hot oil poured over the top.
why_it_works: Oats addition raises fiber meaningfully above a plain besan dhokla
Still steamed, keeping added fat low
Distinct from the plain Besan Dhokla Bites recipe by both ingredient and fiber profile

name: ZITLAS Egg Paneer Combo Bhurji
description: Scrambled egg and crumbled paneer cooked together in one pan — combining two protein sources directly in the bhurji itself, not as separate dishes.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add turmeric and chilli powder.
Add crumbled paneer and cook 2 minutes.
Beat the egg and pour in, scrambling gently until just set, mixing the paneer through.
Serve hot on its own or with a roti.
why_it_works: Two proteins combined in a single pan rather than served as separate items
Higher protein density than either egg bhurji or paneer bhurji alone
Still a familiar, fast dish to cook

name: ZITLAS Soya Flour Chilla
description: A savoury crepe made from soya flour rather than besan or moong batter — a different protein-forward flour base for people who've had enough besan chilla.
instructions: Whisk soya flour and rice flour with water into a smooth, thin batter.
Mix in onion, cumin seeds and green chilli.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread thin.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until crisp on both sides.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Soya flour has a notably higher protein percentage than besan
Different base flour keeps the chilla rotation from feeling repetitive
Very quick, single-pan preparation

name: ZITLAS Roasted Chana Ladoo Bites
description: No-bake bites made from roasted chana flour, jaggery and a little ghee — a besan-free alternative to the peanut chikki bites, portable for a rushed morning.
ingredients: Roasted chana flour (bhuna chana powder) — 100 g
instructions: Melt ghee in a kadai on low heat, add the roasted chana flour and roast for 3-4 minutes until aromatic.
Add jaggery and stir until it melts and combines fully into a thick, moist dough.
Cool slightly, then shape into 8 small balls while still warm.
Store in an airtight container for up to a week.
why_it_works: Different base ingredient from the peanut chikki bites, giving genuine variety among grab-and-go options
Roasted chana flour brings meaningfully more protein than plain flour ladoos
Batch-made once for the whole week

name: ZITLAS Curd Oats Bowl with Roasted Seeds
description: Cold curd mixed with soaked oats and topped with a mix of roasted seeds — a savoury, tangy no-cook bowl distinct from the sweet chia jar or smoothie bowl.
ingredients: Roasted cumin powder, black salt — 2 g
instructions: Soak the oats in a little water for 10 minutes to soften.
Drain any excess water and mix the oats into the curd.
Season with roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Top with mixed roasted seeds just before eating for crunch.
why_it_works: Savoury profile is a genuinely different use of oats from the usual sweet preparations
Seeds on top keep some crunch instead of everything going soft
Zero cooking involved

name: ZITLAS Methi Paneer Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with paneer and fresh fenugreek (methi) leaves — a fiber-and-micronutrient-forward filling distinct from a plain paneer stuffing.
instructions: Mix paneer with chopped methi leaves, ajwain and chilli powder into a filling.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the paneer-methi mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Methi adds iron and a distinct bitterness that plain paneer parathas don't have
Different vegetable pairing from the Lite Paneer Paratha in Batch 1
Traditional winter-season combination

name: ZITLAS Egg Bhurji Rice Bowl
description: Spiced scrambled egg served over warm rice instead of bread or roti — a rice-bowl format for people who prefer rice at any meal.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add turmeric and chilli powder.
Beat the egg and pour in, scrambling until just cooked.
Warm the cooked rice separately (or use leftover rice).
Spoon the bhurji over the rice in a bowl and serve.
why_it_works: Rice-bowl format suits users who find bread or roti heavy in the morning
Also works well with leftover rice, doubling as a leftover-friendly option
Quick and familiar flavours in a different presentation

name: ZITLAS Khakhra Peanut Butter Stack
description: Multigrain khakhra crackers spread with peanut butter and stacked — a genuinely no-cook, no-cleanup hostel breakfast using a shelf-stable base.
instructions: Spread peanut butter evenly over each khakhra.
Stack 2-3 khakhras together.
Eat immediately — khakhra stays crisp only briefly once spread.
why_it_works: Both ingredients are shelf-stable, no refrigeration needed at all
Zero cooking, zero cleanup — just a spoon
Genuinely different texture (crisp) from most no-cook options which are soft

name: ZITLAS Steamed Moong Handvo
description: A savoury steamed cake made from ground moong dal, rava and vegetables — a baked/steamed slice format, distinct from any crepe, roll or paratha in the database.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 100 g
Eno fruit salt, mustard seeds — 4 g
instructions: Mix ground moong dal, rava, curd and grated carrot into a thick batter; rest 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a small baking tin.
Add eno fruit salt just before baking and mix gently.
Pour into the tin, temper mustard seeds in hot oil and pour over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until a knife comes out clean.
Cool slightly and cut into slices.
why_it_works: Cake-slice format is genuinely different from every crepe or roll elsewhere in the database
Bakes in one tin with minimal active attention
Good for a family breakfast cut into shared slices

name: ZITLAS Chicken Keema Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with spiced lean chicken mince — a non-vegetarian counterpart to the vegetarian soya keema paratha, using real meat for users who want it.
instructions: Cook the chicken mince with onion, ginger-garlic paste and garam masala in a pan until fully cooked through and fairly dry; cool slightly.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the cooked mince filling and seal well.
Roll out carefully and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden and cooked through on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Genuine non-vegetarian option for users who prefer real meat over a soya substitute
Lean mince keeps fat moderate while protein stays high
Filling must be fully pre-cooked, which also makes the paratha safer and quicker to roast

name: ZITLAS Oat Flour Paneer Kathi Roll
description: A roti made from oat flour instead of wheat, rolled around a spiced paneer filling kathi-roll style — swaps the base grain rather than the filling.
instructions: Mix oat flour with a small amount of wheat atta (oat flour alone doesn't bind well) and knead into a dough.
Roll out and roast on a tawa until light brown spots appear.
Dry-toss paneer with onion and chaat masala.
Lay the filling on the roti, roll tightly, and serve.
why_it_works: Oat-flour base changes the fiber and glycemic profile of the roti itself, not just the filling
Different construction technique from any other paneer recipe in the database
Still eats like a familiar kathi roll

name: ZITLAS Tofu Ginger-Soy Scramble Wrap
description: Crumbled tofu scrambled with ginger and soy sauce in an Indo-Chinese style, rolled into a wrap — a distinctly different spice profile from the Indian-masala tofu bhurji toast.
instructions: Roll out the atta into a roti and roast on a tawa; keep warm.
Heat oil, saute ginger and garlic, then add crumbled tofu and soy sauce, stirring for 4-5 minutes.
Finish with chopped spring onion.
Spread the tofu scramble onto the roti and roll up tightly.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Indo-Chinese seasoning gives a genuinely different flavour direction from Indian-spiced tofu elsewhere in the database
Fully vegan, high protein
Quick one-pan filling

name: ZITLAS Makhana Peanut Trail Mix Bowl
description: A dry, portable mix of roasted makhana and peanuts with a few raisins — a crunchy grab-and-go bowl distinct from the yogurt-based makhana parfait.
instructions: Combine roasted makhana, peanuts and raisins in a small container.
Mix well.
Carry in the container and eat on the move, or as a sit-down bowl.
why_it_works: Entirely dry format, unlike the yogurt-based makhana parfait, so it travels without spoilage risk
Genuinely no prep beyond mixing
Good option when there's no fridge access

name: ZITLAS Green Moong Soup Bowl
description: A warm, lightly spiced moong dal soup eaten as a savoury liquid breakfast — an unusual soup format rather than a solid dish.
instructions: Pressure cook moong dal with tomato and enough water for 3 whistles until fully soft.
Blend lightly or mash for a smoother, soup-like consistency.
Heat oil, temper cumin seeds and garlic, and pour into the soup.
Season with black pepper and simmer 3-4 minutes.
Serve hot in a mug or bowl, sipped like a soup.
why_it_works: Soup format is genuinely different from every solid breakfast in the database
Very light on the stomach for people who don't want to chew much in the morning
Simple one-pot preparation

name: ZITLAS Paneer Stuffed Idli
description: Regular idli batter poured over a small spiced paneer filling in the mould, so the protein is steamed inside the idli itself rather than served alongside.
instructions: Mix crumbled paneer with chopped coriander and green chilli.
Grease the idli moulds and add a small spoon of batter to each.
Place a small portion of the paneer mixture in the centre, then cover with more batter to fully enclose it.
Steam for 10-12 minutes in a pressure cooker without the whistle.
Serve hot with chutney or sambar.
why_it_works: Protein is steamed inside the idli rather than served as a side, unlike the Protein-Boosted Idli Sambar in Batch 1
Fun surprise-filling format that works well for families and kids too
Still fully steamed, no added oil

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Rava Idli
description: Steamed semolina idli with grated vegetables mixed directly into the batter — no fermentation needed, ready much faster than regular idli.
ingredients: Eno fruit salt, mustard seeds — 4 g
instructions: Dry-roast rava lightly, then mix with curd, grated carrot, peas and a little water into a thick batter; rest 10 minutes.
Add eno fruit salt just before steaming.
Pour into greased idli moulds and steam for 10-12 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds in oil and drizzle over the idlis before serving.
why_it_works: No fermentation wait, so it's ready much faster than dal-based idli
Vegetables mixed directly into the batter, not a side garnish
Distinct base grain from every other idli variant in the database

name: ZITLAS Soya Sabzi Roti Roll
description: A wet, gravy-style soya chunk sabzi rolled inside a roti — distinct from the dry keema-style filling and the frankie's masala-dusted soya.
instructions: Roll out and roast the atta into rotis; keep warm.
Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cook until soft.
Add soya chunks and garam masala with a splash of water, simmer 8-10 minutes into a slightly wet sabzi.
Spoon the sabzi onto a roti and roll (or fold), letting some gravy soak into the bread.
Serve immediately while warm.
why_it_works: Gravy-style filling gives a distinctly different eating experience — softer, saucier — from the other dry soya rolls in the database
Uses the same soya base as other recipes but a genuinely different cooking method
Filling, homely breakfast

name: ZITLAS Curd Rice Balls
description: Portion-sized curd rice shaped into small balls — a portable, lunchbox-ready version of the usual bowl-format curd rice.
instructions: Mash the cold rice with curd until well combined and slightly sticky.
Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and peanuts in oil and mix into the rice.
Once cool enough to handle, shape into 4-5 small balls.
Pack into a small container — they hold their shape for a few hours.
why_it_works: Ball format is genuinely more portable than the usual curd rice bowl
No last-minute assembly needed once packed
Works well for a mid-morning lunchbox snack rather than a sit-down breakfast

name: ZITLAS Egg Bhurji Pav
description: Mumbai-style spiced scrambled egg stuffed into a soft pav bun — a bun-sandwich format distinct from a roti roll or toast.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add pav bhaji masala.
Beat the egg and pour in, scrambling until just cooked.
Slice the pav bun and lightly toast the cut sides on the tawa with a touch of butter or oil.
Stuff the egg bhurji into the pav.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Pav bun format is a genuinely different bread base from roti, toast or paratha elsewhere in the database
Mumbai street-food flavour angle keeps the spicing distinct
Fast, familiar comfort food

name: ZITLAS Multi-Millet Savoury Porridge
description: A blended multi-millet flour cooked into a savoury porridge with vegetables — different from any single-millet upma by using a flour blend rather than whole grain.
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then saute finely chopped vegetables for 2-3 minutes.
Add water and bring to a simmer.
Whisk in the multi-millet flour gradually to avoid lumps, stirring continuously.
Simmer 6-8 minutes until it thickens to a porridge consistency, then serve hot.
why_it_works: Flour-blend format cooks faster than whole-grain millet upma
Combines the fiber benefits of several millets rather than just one
Warm, comforting texture for cooler mornings

name: ZITLAS Paneer Palak Toast
description: Mashed paneer mixed with cooked spinach, spread over toasted bread — a green, iron-rich spread format distinct from bhurji or toast dips.
instructions: Heat oil, saute garlic briefly, then add spinach and cook until wilted, about 3 minutes.
Mash the paneer into the cooked spinach, mixing until it forms a spreadable mixture.
Toast the bread slices.
Spread the paneer-palak mixture over the toast and season with black pepper.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Spread format is a genuinely different toast preparation from the besan-battered toast in Batch 1
Spinach adds iron and fiber not present in most other paneer dishes here
Quick and visually different (green) from other toasts

name: ZITLAS Sprout Peanut Salad Cup
description: A no-cook, portion-cup salad of sprouts and crushed peanuts dressed with lemon — packed the night before for a genuinely zero-morning-effort breakfast.
instructions: Rinse and drain the sprouts well.
Toss with crushed peanuts, lemon juice and chaat masala.
Pack into a sealed cup or container the night before.
Eat straight from the container in the morning — no reheating or assembly needed.
why_it_works: Explicitly designed to be assembled the night before, unlike other no-cook recipes eaten immediately
Zero morning effort at all beyond opening the container
Very low cost, very portable

name: ZITLAS Baked Sweet Potato with Curd
description: An oven-baked sweet potato split open and topped with curd and crushed peanuts — a grain-free breakfast base built around a root vegetable instead.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and bake the whole sweet potato for 20-25 minutes until soft when pierced.
Split it open lengthwise.
Top with curd and crushed peanuts.
Sprinkle chaat masala and serve warm.
why_it_works: Genuinely grain-free breakfast base, unusual in an Indian breakfast context
Sweet potato brings fiber and beta-carotene that grain bases don't
Very simple, mostly hands-off oven cooking

name: ZITLAS Egg Curry Rice Bowl
description: A rice bowl topped with the same light egg curry used in the roti version, but served over rice instead — a distinct pairing from the Egg Curry with Multigrain Roti recipe.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cook until pulpy.
Add garam masala and a little water to form a light gravy; simmer 5 minutes.
Halve the boiled eggs and simmer in the gravy for 2-3 minutes.
Serve the egg curry ladled over warm rice in a bowl.
why_it_works: Rice-bowl pairing is a genuinely different meal format from the roti version, suiting rice-preference households
Same curry technique reused efficiently, but the eating experience differs meaningfully
One-pan gravy, minimal cleanup

name: ZITLAS Chana Chaat Toast
description: A tangy boiled-chana chaat piled directly onto toasted bread — combines a chaat and a toast into one dish rather than serving them separately.
instructions: Toast the bread slices lightly.
Toss boiled chana with onion, tomato, lemon juice and chaat masala in a bowl.
Pile the chana chaat generously onto the toast.
Eat immediately with a fork before the toast softens.
why_it_works: Combining chaat and toast into one dish is a distinct format from either eaten separately
High fiber and protein for very low cost
Fast to assemble with almost no active cooking

name: ZITLAS Moong Cheela Mini Pizza
description: A moong dal cheela base topped like a mini pizza with tomato, onion, capsicum and grated paneer, then briefly covered to melt — a playful, family-friendly format.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 60 g
instructions: Cook the moong dal batter into a thick round cheela base on the tawa, as usual, but only on one side.
Flip so the uncooked side faces up, then scatter tomato, capsicum and grated paneer over the top.
Cover with a lid and cook on low heat for 3-4 minutes so the toppings soften and the paneer softens slightly.
Sprinkle oregano and chilli flakes, slice like a pizza, and serve.
why_it_works: Playful topped format makes it distinctly different from a folded or rolled cheela
Kid-friendly presentation without losing the protein content
One pan, no oven needed unlike a real pizza

name: ZITLAS Soya Stuffed Pav
description: Spiced soya granules stuffed into a pav bun, Mumbai vada-pav-style but with soya replacing the usual potato filling.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, turmeric, green chilli — 3 g
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, add onion and green chilli, saute until soft.
Add rehydrated soya granules and turmeric, cook 4-5 minutes until well coated and slightly dry.
Slice the pav and lightly toast the cut sides.
Stuff the soya mixture generously into the pav.
Serve with a side of green chutney.
why_it_works: Familiar vada-pav format but with a higher-protein, lower-oil filling than the traditional potato vada
Different bread base from any roti-based soya recipe in the database
Genuinely street-food-inspired without deep frying

name: ZITLAS Ragi Malt Drink
description: A traditional Karnataka-style fermented-style ragi malt porridge drink, sipped from a glass — a liquid finger-millet format distinct from ragi dosa or rajgira porridge.
instructions: Whisk ragi flour into a little cold water to avoid lumps.
Bring the rest of the water to a boil, add the ragi mixture, and simmer 6-8 minutes, stirring often, until it thickens slightly and loses its raw smell.
Cool to room temperature, then whisk in buttermilk and cumin powder.
Pour into a glass and drink — this is a savoury, sippable porridge, not a thick bowl.
why_it_works: Liquid, sippable format is distinct from every solid ragi or millet dish in the database
Very cooling and light, suited to hot mornings
Traditional South Indian drink genuinely different from a smoothie

name: ZITLAS Paneer Bhurji Kulcha
description: Spiced paneer bhurji stuffed inside a kulcha instead of a roti or paratha — a different bread base with its own texture and flavour.
instructions: Knead refined flour with curd and a little water into a soft kulcha dough; rest 15 minutes.
Mix paneer with onion and chaat masala for the filling.
Roll out the dough, stuff with the paneer filling and seal.
Roast on a hot tawa with a little oil until golden with brown spots on both sides.
Serve hot with pickle.
why_it_works: Kulcha dough (with curd) has a distinctly softer, richer texture from a plain wheat roti or paratha
Different bread technique broadens the database's bread formats beyond roti/paratha
Restaurant-style comfort food made at home

name: ZITLAS Leftover Rice Egg Fried Rice Bowl
description: Leftover rice and egg stir-fried Indo-Chinese style with vegetables — a genuinely different leftover-rice recipe from the Maharashtrian-style protein poha version in Batch 1.
ingredients: Soy sauce, garlic, spring onion — 6 g
instructions: Heat oil in a kadai on high heat, saute garlic and vegetables for 2 minutes.
Push to one side, crack in the egg and scramble it in the empty space.
Add the cold leftover rice and soy sauce, tossing everything together on high heat for 3-4 minutes.
Finish with chopped spring onion and serve hot.
why_it_works: Indo-Chinese flavour direction is genuinely different from the tempered, turmeric-based leftover rice poha in Batch 1
High-heat tossing gives a different texture (slightly charred) from a softer poha-style dish
Uses cold rice specifically, working better than fresh rice for this technique

name: ZITLAS Curd Chilla
description: A besan chilla batter enriched with whisked curd for extra protein and a softer texture — a variant that changes the batter itself, not the filling.
instructions: Whisk besan with curd, water, turmeric and cumin seeds into a smooth batter (curd replaces some of the water used in a plain chilla).
Mix in chopped onion.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a round.
Drizzle a little oil and cook until golden on both sides.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Curd in the batter itself raises protein above a plain besan chilla without adding a separate filling step
Softer, slightly tangier texture than the usual water-based chilla
Still a one-pan, quick preparation

name: ZITLAS Boiled Egg Curry Wrap
description: A drier version of egg curry, thickened and reduced, wrapped inside a roti instead of eaten with rice or a separate roti — a wrap format for the same base curry technique.
instructions: Roll out and roast the atta into a roti; keep warm.
Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cook until dry and thick (less liquid than the bowl versions).
Chop the boiled eggs and mix into the thick masala, coating well without excess gravy.
Spoon onto the roti and roll tightly so it doesn't leak.
Wrap in foil and serve.
why_it_works: Deliberately drier consistency than the two curry-bowl versions, specifically so it holds together as a wrap
Third genuinely different way to eat the same egg-curry base across the database — bowl with roti, bowl with rice, and now a wrap
Portable for a commute

name: ZITLAS Matki Usal Bowl
description: A Maharashtrian-style sprouted moth bean (matki) usal, tempered and simmered — using a legume not used elsewhere in the database for genuine protein-source diversity.
ingredients: Goda masala or garam masala — 4 g
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add tomato and cook until soft.
Add the boiled sprouted matki and goda masala, mixing well.
Add a little water and simmer 6-8 minutes until the flavours combine.
Serve hot as a bowl, with a squeeze of lemon if liked.
why_it_works: Matki is a distinct legume from moong, chana or rajma already used across the database
Traditional Maharashtrian usal reframed as a protein-forward breakfast rather than a side dish
One-pan, genuinely regional

name: ZITLAS Paneer Corn Tikki
description: Pan-fried patties combining crumbled paneer with boiled corn kernels — a distinct filling combination from any other tikki or cutlet in the database.
instructions: Mash paneer with boiled corn, onion, coriander and green chilli into a coarse mixture.
Shape into 3-4 small tikkis.
Pan-fry in oil until golden on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Corn adds natural sweetness and a distinct texture not present in other tikki recipes here
Kid-friendly flavour profile suits family breakfasts
Different filling combination from the sprout-paneer or moong-dal tikkis

name: ZITLAS No-Bake Atta Ladoo Bites
description: No-bake bites made from roasted whole wheat flour, ghee and jaggery — a wheat-based grab-and-go option distinct from the chana-flour and peanut versions.
instructions: Roast the atta in ghee on low heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring continuously, until it turns golden and smells nutty.
Add jaggery and mix until it melts in fully.
Cool slightly, then shape into 8 small balls while still warm.
Store in an airtight container for up to a week.
why_it_works: Third distinct base flour among the ladoo-style bites in the database (wheat, not besan or chana flour)
Very low ingredient count, easy to batch cook
Traditional winter combination made portion-sized

name: ZITLAS Soya Milk Ragi Porridge
description: Ragi flour cooked into a warm porridge using soya milk instead of dairy milk — a fully vegan pairing distinct from the dairy-based rajgira porridge.
instructions: Whisk ragi flour into a little cold soya milk to avoid lumps.
Heat the rest of the soya milk, add the ragi mixture and stir continuously.
Simmer 6-8 minutes until thickened.
Stir in jaggery and cardamom powder, cook 1-2 more minutes, and serve warm.
why_it_works: Fully dairy-free pairing, unlike the milk-based Rajgira Milk Porridge earlier in this batch
Ragi's calcium content pairs well with soya milk's protein for a vegan-complete combination
Good option for lactose-intolerant users

name: ZITLAS Leftover Dal Rice Cutlets
description: Leftover toor dal and leftover rice mashed together and shaped into pan-fried cutlets — rescues two different leftovers at once in a single dish.
instructions: Mash the leftover dal and rice together with onion and spices.
Add a little rice flour if the mixture feels too wet to hold shape.
Shape into small cutlets.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp and golden on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve with ketchup or chutney.
why_it_works: Rescues two separate leftovers — dal and rice — in one dish, unlike single-leftover recipes elsewhere in the database
Crisping via pan-frying gives a genuinely different texture from just reheating either leftover
Very low additional cost since the base is already cooked

name: ZITLAS Greek Yogurt Chilla Crumble Bowl
description: A besan chilla is torn into pieces and layered into a bowl with Greek yogurt and chutney, deconstructed rather than served as a whole crepe.
instructions: Whisk besan with water and cumin seeds into a batter and cook a thin chilla on a tawa as usual.
Once cooked, tear the chilla into bite-sized pieces rather than rolling or folding it.
Layer the torn chilla pieces in a bowl with Greek yogurt and a drizzle of mint chutney.
Mix gently just before eating, like a deconstructed chaat.
why_it_works: Deconstructed bowl format is a genuinely different eating experience from every rolled or folded chilla elsewhere in the database
Greek yogurt adds meaningfully more protein than curd would
Fun, chaat-like way to eat a familiar base

name: ZITLAS Paneer Tikka Skewers
description: Paneer cubes marinated in curd and spices, grilled on skewers — a tikka format eaten as breakfast rather than an evening starter.
instructions: Marinate paneer, capsicum and onion cubes in curd and tikka masala for at least 15 minutes.
Thread onto skewers, alternating paneer and vegetables.
Grill in an oven or air fryer at 200°C for 10-12 minutes, turning once, until lightly charred.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Grilled, not fried — very little added oil
Skewer format is genuinely different from any bhurji, roll or toast in the database
High protein for a light breakfast

name: ZITLAS Moong Cheela Veg Taco Fold
description: A moong dal cheela folded taco-style around a fresh, no-cook vegetable salsa — the filling is raw and crunchy rather than cooked.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 60 g
instructions: Cook the moong dal batter into a small, sturdy round on the tawa (thicker than a regular cheela so it holds a fold).
Toss tomato, onion and cucumber with lemon juice and coriander for a fresh salsa.
Fold the warm cheela in half like a taco shell and spoon in the raw salsa just before eating so it stays crisp.
Eat immediately.
why_it_works: Combining a cooked base with a raw, no-cook filling is a distinct format from every other cheela in the database
Very fresh, crunchy texture contrast
Light and low-calorie

name: ZITLAS Baked Vegetable Frittata Slice
description: A single large egg-and-vegetable frittata baked in one pan and cut into slices — different from individual muffin cups, meant to be sliced and shared or portioned.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C and grease a round baking dish.
Saute onion, capsicum and spinach in oil for 3-4 minutes until slightly softened.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper, then pour over the vegetables in the greased dish.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until fully set and lightly golden on top.
Cool slightly, slice like a pie, and serve.
why_it_works: One large bake serves multiple people, unlike single-portion muffin cups
Slices reheat well for a couple of days
Good option for a shared family breakfast

name: ZITLAS Chana Pulao Bowl
description: A lightly spiced rice pulao cooked with boiled chana — a warm rice-and-legume breakfast bowl, distinct from a khichdi or curry-rice pairing.
ingredients: Whole spices (bay leaf, cumin), garam masala — 4 g
instructions: Heat oil, temper whole spices, then saute onion until golden.
Add rice and boiled chana, along with garam masala, mixing well.
Add water in the standard rice ratio and pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.
why_it_works: Pulao format (whole grains of rice, not mushy like khichdi) is a genuinely different texture from other rice-legume dishes here
One-pot, mostly hands-off cooking
Filling for a mid-morning appetite

name: ZITLAS Chana Masala Toast Boats
description: Whole wheat bread rolls hollowed out and filled with a scoop of hot chana masala — a boat format distinct from a flat toast topping.
ingredients: Chana masala powder, ginger-garlic paste — 5 g
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cook until soft.
Add boiled chana and chana masala powder with a little water; simmer 8-10 minutes into a thick masala.
Slice the top off each bread roll and hollow out some of the inside to make a boat.
Spoon the hot chana masala into the bread boats and serve immediately.
why_it_works: Boat format holds a wet curry without making the bread soggy the way a flat toast topping would
Fun, different presentation of a familiar chana masala
High fiber from chana and bread combined

name: ZITLAS Roasted Flaxseed Peanut Bites
description: No-bake bites made from roasted flaxseed powder and peanuts bound with jaggery — a different seed base from the chikki or ladoo bites elsewhere, adding an omega-3 angle.
instructions: Melt jaggery with ghee in a kadai on low heat until syrupy.
Turn off heat, quickly mix in ground flaxseed and crushed peanuts, coating evenly.
Shape into 8 small balls while still warm.
Cool completely and store in an airtight container for up to a week.
why_it_works: Flaxseed brings a fiber and omega-3 profile that the peanut-only or besan-only bites in the database don't have
Genuinely different base ingredient, not just a renamed chikki
Batch-made for the week

name: ZITLAS Paneer Stuffed Naan Bites
description: Small naan breads stuffed with spiced paneer and cooked in a pan — a naan-based format, distinct from roti, kulcha or paratha stuffing elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Knead maida with curd, a pinch of baking soda and water into a soft dough; rest 20 minutes.
Mix paneer with onion and chaat masala for the filling.
Divide the dough into small balls, stuff each with a little filling and seal.
Flatten gently and roast on a hot tawa with a little oil until golden spots appear on both sides.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Naan dough (with curd and baking soda) has a distinctly softer, puffier texture from a plain wheat dough
Bite-sized format works well for sharing or a lunchbox
Broadens the bread formats in the database beyond roti/paratha/kulcha

name: ZITLAS Egg Drop Vegetable Soup Bowl
description: A light vegetable broth with beaten egg dropped in ribbons, Indo-Chinese style — a savoury liquid breakfast built around egg rather than dal.
ingredients: Garlic, black pepper, soy sauce — 5 g
instructions: Heat oil, saute garlic and finely chopped vegetables for 2 minutes.
Add water and bring to a gentle boil; simmer 5 minutes.
Season with black pepper and soy sauce.
Beat the egg and pour in slowly in a thin stream while stirring, so it forms ribbons.
Serve hot in a bowl.
why_it_works: Egg-based soup format is distinct from the dal-based Green Moong Soup Bowl elsewhere in the database
Very light, good for a low-appetite morning
Quick, one-pot preparation

name: ZITLAS Sprouted Chana Chaat Bowl
description: Raw sprouted chana (not boiled) tossed with onion, tomato and lemon — a crunchier, no-cook alternative to boiled-chana-based chaats.
ingredients: Sprouted chana (raw sprouts, not boiled) — 100 g
instructions: Rinse the sprouted chana well.
Toss with onion, tomato, lemon juice and chaat masala.
Eat immediately for maximum crunch — sprouted chana softens if left standing.
why_it_works: Sprouted (raw) rather than boiled chana keeps a distinctly crunchier bite than the boiled versions used elsewhere
Entirely no-cook
High fiber, low calorie

name: ZITLAS Stuffed Multigrain Dosa
description: A multigrain dosa filled with a spiced paneer masala and folded closed — a stuffed dosa format distinct from a plain or topped dosa.
instructions: Mix multigrain flour into the fermented dosa batter.
Heat oil, saute onion until soft, add paneer, turmeric and chilli powder, cook 3-4 minutes for the filling.
Pour the batter on a hot tawa and spread into a dosa.
Once mostly cooked, place the paneer filling on one half and fold the dosa over.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Stuffed-and-folded construction is a genuinely different eating experience from a flat or topped dosa
Multigrain flour raises fiber above a plain rice-urad dosa
Filling protein source keeps this distinct from the plain Ragi Dosa or Vegetable Rava Idli

name: ZITLAS Dahi Poha
description: Cold flattened rice soaked directly in whisked curd with a light tempering — a chilled poha format, distinct from the hot tempered kanda poha or leftover rice poha.
instructions: Rinse the poha briefly and let it soften, then mix directly into whisked curd.
Add finely chopped onion and mix.
Quickly temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in a little hot oil and pour over the top.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
why_it_works: Cold, curd-based format is a genuinely different eating experience from hot tempered poha
Very light and cooling, good for hot weather
Almost no active cooking

name: ZITLAS Oats Banana Pancake Stack
description: Griddle-cooked pancakes made from a blended oats-and-banana batter, stacked like a Western-style pancake breakfast but without refined flour or added sugar.
instructions: Blend oats, banana, milk and egg together into a smooth, pourable batter.
Heat a lightly greased tawa and pour small rounds of batter, cooking 2 minutes per side until golden.
Stack 3-4 small pancakes.
Serve as is — the banana provides sweetness without any added sugar.
why_it_works: Griddle-pancake format is genuinely different from the smoothie bowl or porridge oats already in the database
No refined flour or added sugar, unlike a typical pancake
Naturally sweetened only by banana

name: ZITLAS Masala Poha Cutlet
description: Leftover cooked poha shaped into pan-fried cutlets — a genuinely different leftover-rescue recipe using leftover poha rather than rice, roti or dal.
instructions: Mash the leftover poha lightly with onion, rice flour and spices until it holds together.
Shape into small flat cutlets.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp and golden on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve with ketchup or chutney.
why_it_works: Genuinely rescues leftover poha specifically, a food-waste angle not covered elsewhere in the database
Crisping via pan-frying gives a completely different texture from reheated poha
Very low additional cost

name: ZITLAS Bengali Fish Curry Rice Bowl
description: A light Bengali-style fish curry served over warm rice — a regional non-vegetarian breakfast using fish, a protein source not used elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Rub the fish fillet with turmeric and a little salt.
Heat mustard oil, temper panch phoron, then saute onion until soft.
Add tomato and cook until pulpy, then add a little water to form a light gravy.
Gently add the fish and simmer 6-8 minutes until just cooked through, being careful not to break it up.
Serve the curry over warm rice.
