why_it_works: Fish is a distinct protein source from every other recipe in the database, giving genuine variety for non-vegetarian users
Mustard oil and panch phoron give an authentic Bengali flavour base
Light gravy keeps this suited to a fitness-conscious breakfast rather than a heavy lunch curry

name: ZITLAS Paneer Bhurji Stuffed Capsicum
description: Capsicum halves stuffed with spiced paneer bhurji and lightly steamed — a vegetable-as-vessel format distinct from any bread, rice or roll pairing.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion, add turmeric and chilli powder, then add paneer and cook 3-4 minutes into a bhurji.
Stuff the paneer bhurji generously into the capsicum halves.
Steam the stuffed capsicum halves in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 6-8 minutes until the capsicum softens slightly but keeps some bite.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Using the vegetable itself as the vessel removes the need for bread or rice entirely
Lower carb than most other paneer bhurji pairings in the database
Visually different, good for a lighter breakfast

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Bread Upma
description: Day-old bread torn into pieces and tossed upma-style with a mustard-curry leaf tempering and vegetables — a bread-based upma distinct from the rava, poha or dalia versions.
ingredients: Whole wheat bread, torn into pieces — 90 g
Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then saute onion and tomato until soft.
Add turmeric and the torn bread pieces, tossing gently on medium heat for 3-4 minutes until well coated and slightly crisp at the edges.
Serve hot immediately, before the bread softens too much.
why_it_works: Uses leftover or day-old bread that would otherwise be wasted, a distinct leftover-rescue angle from the rice, roti or poha versions
Familiar upma tempering technique applied to an unusual base
Very fast, one-pan preparation

name: ZITLAS Soya Chunk Salad Bowl
description: Cold, marinated soya chunks tossed with vegetables in a no-cook salad — distinct from the cooked soya sabzi, frankie or keema preparations elsewhere.
ingredients: Soya chunks, boiled and cooled — 80 g
instructions: Boil the soya chunks briefly, squeeze out excess water, and let cool completely.
Toss the cooled soya chunks with cucumber and tomato.
Dress with lemon juice, a little oil, black pepper and chaat masala.
Chill briefly if possible and serve cold.
why_it_works: Cold salad format is a genuinely different way to eat soya chunks from every cooked preparation elsewhere in the database
No stovetop cooking needed at breakfast time if chunks are pre-boiled the night before
High protein, low calorie

name: ZITLAS Dahi Semiya (Curd Vermicelli)
description: Cooked vermicelli mixed cold into whisked curd with a light tempering — a South Indian cold noodle-like breakfast dish.
instructions: Boil the vermicelli until just tender, drain and cool completely.
Mix the cooled vermicelli into whisked curd along with grated carrot.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot oil and pour over the top.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
why_it_works: Cold, curd-based format is genuinely different from the hot Soya Vermicelli Upma in Batch 2
Light and cooling, suited to hot mornings
Simple, familiar South Indian home food

name: ZITLAS Egg Bhurji Dosa
description: Spiced scrambled egg folded inside a plain dosa — combining two familiar breakfast items into one, distinct from a plain or vegetable dosa.
instructions: Saute onion in a little oil, add turmeric and chilli powder, then scramble in the beaten egg until just set; set aside.
Pour dosa batter on a hot tawa and spread into a dosa.
While the top is still slightly wet, spread the cooked egg bhurji over half of it and fold the dosa over.
Cook briefly to crisp the outside, then serve.
why_it_works: Combines two familiar dishes into a single distinct format, different from a plain dosa or a separate egg bhurji
Higher protein than a plain or vegetable dosa
Popular street-food-style combination

name: ZITLAS Peanut Butter Banana Roti Roll
description: A whole wheat roti spread with peanut butter and sliced banana, rolled up — a sweet roll format distinct from the savoury rolls elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Roll out the atta into a roti and dry-roast on a tawa until just cooked, without over-browning.
Spread peanut butter evenly over the warm roti.
Lay banana slices along one edge and roll up tightly.
Slice in half and serve.
why_it_works: First genuinely sweet roll in the database — most rolls are savoury
No refined sugar, sweetened only by banana
Very quick, minimal ingredients

name: ZITLAS Rajma Chaat Bowl
description: Boiled rajma tossed chaat-style with onion, tomato and tangy spices — a cold, no-cook bowl distinct from the cooked rajma paratha or tikki sandwich elsewhere.
instructions: Toss boiled rajma with onion and tomato.
Add lemon juice and chaat masala.
Mix well and eat immediately while the onion stays crisp.
why_it_works: No-cook chaat format is a genuinely different way to eat rajma from the two cooked recipes already in the database
High fiber, filling, and very low active prep time
Good for a rushed morning

name: ZITLAS Paneer Achari Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha with paneer filling spiced with pickle (achaari) masala — a tangy, distinct spice profile from the other paneer parathas in the database.
ingredients: Pickle masala (achaari) or mustard oil pickle spice mix — 8 g
instructions: Mix paneer with onion and achaari pickle masala into a tangy, spiced filling.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the filling and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Pickle-spiced (achaari) profile is a distinctly different flavour direction from methi, lite or beetroot paneer parathas elsewhere in the database
Tangy spicing needs less added salt or chutney on the side
Popular restaurant-style flavour made at home

name: ZITLAS Moong Dal Dhokla
description: A steamed dhokla made from ground moong dal instead of besan or oats — a different pulse base with its own dense, slightly nutty texture.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 120 g
instructions: Grind soaked moong dal with curd and a little water into a thick batter; rest 15 minutes.
Add eno fruit salt just before steaming and mix gently.
Pour into a greased tin and steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 12-15 minutes.
Cool slightly, cut into squares, and temper mustard and sesame seeds in oil poured over the top.
why_it_works: Moong dal delivers meaningfully more protein per serving than a besan-based dhokla
Distinctly denser texture from the lighter besan or oats versions
Steamed, low added fat

name: ZITLAS Sattu Ladoo Bites
description: No-bake bites made from sattu, jaggery and ghee — a solid, portable format distinct from the sattu drink and sattu-curd bowl elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Melt ghee in a kadai on low heat, add sattu and roast for 2-3 minutes until aromatic.
Add jaggery and mix until fully combined into a thick, moist dough.
Cool slightly, then shape into 8 small balls while still warm.
Store in an airtight container for up to a week.
why_it_works: Solid, portable bite format is genuinely different from the drink or bowl formats already using sattu in the database
Very cheap, high-protein grab-and-go option
Batch-made once for the week

name: ZITLAS Soya Chunk Biryani Bowl
description: Rice and soya chunks layered and cooked dum-style with biryani spices — a distinct spice profile and format from the plain pulao or brown rice meal-prep bowl.
instructions: Marinate the rehydrated soya chunks in curd and biryani masala for 10 minutes.
Heat oil, fry sliced onion until golden and set aside half for garnish.
Layer partially-cooked rice with the marinated soya and remaining fried onion in the cooker.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat (dum-style) for 12-15 minutes.
Fluff gently and garnish with the reserved fried onion before serving.
why_it_works: Biryani spicing and dum technique give a distinctly different flavour and texture from the pulao or plain rice-soya recipes elsewhere
Layered cooking method is a genuinely different technique from a one-pot khichdi or pulao
Weekend-special feel while staying vegetarian and high-protein

name: ZITLAS Paneer Frankie Roll
description: A Mumbai-style frankie roll filled with spiced paneer instead of soya, using the same charred-roti technique but a different protein.
instructions: Roll out and roast the atta into a roti on a tawa until slightly charred at the edges.
Pan-sear paneer cubes with pav bhaji masala until lightly browned.
Spread green and tamarind chutney on the roti, add the paneer and sliced onion.
Roll tightly frankie-style and serve immediately.
why_it_works: Same proven frankie format as the Soya Frankie Roll but with paneer, giving users a protein choice within a familiar format
Two chutneys keep the flavour profile distinct from other paneer rolls in the database
Portable for a commute

name: ZITLAS Lauki Paratha with Curd
description: A stuffed paratha filled with grated bottle gourd (lauki) — a high-water, high-fiber vegetable rarely used in breakfast parathas, served with a side of curd for protein.
ingredients: Bottle gourd (lauki), grated and squeezed — 80 g
instructions: Grate the lauki, squeeze out excess water, and mix with ajwain and chilli powder for the filling.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the lauki mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with a side of curd.
why_it_works: Lauki is a genuinely different vegetable filling from any other paratha in the database — high water content and mild flavour
Very low calorie filling, good for weight-loss goals
Curd on the side supplies the protein the vegetable itself lacks

name: ZITLAS Egg Toastie Sandwich
description: A sealed, grilled sandwich with a thin egg omelette layer between bread slices — a closed toastie format distinct from an open toast or a wrap.
instructions: Beat the egg with onion and black pepper, and cook a thin, bread-sized omelette in a pan.
Sandwich the omelette between two slices of bread.
Lightly grill the whole sandwich on a tawa with a little oil, pressing down, until both sides are golden and crisp.
Slice and serve.
why_it_works: Sealed, pressed toastie format is a genuinely different texture from an open-faced toast or wrap
Portable and mess-free once cooked
Familiar comfort food with high protein

name: ZITLAS Curd Chana Dosa
description: A dosa batter enriched by blending in boiled chana — raising the protein of the batter itself rather than relying on a filling.
instructions: Blend the boiled chana with a little water into a smooth paste, then mix into the fermented dosa batter along with cumin seeds.
Heat a tawa, pour the batter and spread into a dosa.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until crisp, then flip briefly.
Serve hot with chutney.
why_it_works: Protein is blended into the batter itself, unlike the Protein-Boosted Idli Sambar approach which relies on a side dish
Distinctly different from a plain dosa in both protein content and slightly nutty flavour
Still cooks exactly like a familiar dosa

name: ZITLAS Beetroot Paneer Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha with a paneer and grated beetroot filling — an iron-rich, visually distinct pink filling from any other paneer paratha in the database.
instructions: Mix paneer with grated beetroot, cumin powder and chilli powder for the filling.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the beetroot-paneer mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Beetroot brings iron and a distinct earthy sweetness not present in any other paneer filling in the database
Visually distinctive (pink interior), which helps variety for repeat users
Traditional protein source in a genuinely different vegetable pairing

name: ZITLAS Moong Sprouts Uttapam
description: A thick pancake made from ground sprouted (not just soaked) moong dal with vegetables pressed on top — a different base and texture from any other uttapam or dosa.
instructions: Grind the sprouted (not just soaked) moong with a little water and cumin seeds into a thick batter — sprouting gives a slightly different, nuttier flavour than plain soaked dal.
Heat a tawa, pour a thick ladle of batter and spread only slightly.
Scatter onion and tomato over the top and press gently.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until the base is golden, then flip briefly.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Using sprouted rather than soaked moong changes both the nutrition and flavour meaningfully from other moong-based dosas or cheelas
Thick uttapam format holds toppings better than a thin dosa
Naturally gluten-free

name: ZITLAS Roasted Gram Dal Chutney Sandwich
description: A sandwich spread made from roasted chana dal ground into a coconut-free chutney — a distinct spread from the peanut thecha or chana chaat sandwiches elsewhere.
instructions: Blend roasted chana dal with green chilli, garlic, lemon juice and a little water into a thick, spreadable chutney.
Spread generously between two slices of bread.
Serve as is, or lightly toast the sandwich if preferred.
why_it_works: Coconut-free, low-fat chutney spread that's meaningfully different from peanut- or chana-chaat-based sandwich fillings elsewhere
Genuinely no-cook if eaten untoasted
Very cheap protein spread instead of butter or jam

name: ZITLAS Multi-Veg Paratha with Protein Raita
description: A paratha stuffed with a mix of grated vegetables (carrot, cabbage, bottle gourd), specifically paired with a Greek yogurt raita so the protein comes from the side, not the filling.
instructions: Mix the grated vegetables with ajwain and chilli powder, squeezing out excess water first.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the vegetable mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Serve with a generous side of Greek yogurt raita — this is where most of the meal's protein comes from.
why_it_works: Deliberately designed so the protein comes from the raita pairing rather than the filling, a distinct nutritional strategy from the protein-stuffed parathas elsewhere
Uses more than one vegetable in the filling instead of just one
Greek yogurt raises the raita's protein well above regular curd

name: ZITLAS Chicken Bhurji Toast
description: Shredded boiled chicken spiced and scrambled bhurji-style, served over toast — a non-vegetarian bhurji variant using real chicken instead of a soya substitute.
instructions: Boil and shred the chicken breast ahead of time.
Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add turmeric and chilli powder.
Add the shredded chicken and cook 4-5 minutes, breaking it up further into a bhurji-like texture.
Toast the bread and spoon the chicken bhurji over the top.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Genuine lean-meat protein option for non-vegetarian users who want more than eggs at breakfast
Bhurji technique applied to chicken rather than egg, soya or paneer gives real protein-source variety
High protein, low fat when using breast meat

name: ZITLAS Fish Cutlet Sandwich
description: Pan-fried fish cutlets, Kerala-style, sandwiched in toasted bread — a distinct non-vegetarian protein and format from the chicken or egg options elsewhere.
ingredients: Lean fish fillet, boiled and flaked — 100 g
Ginger, green chilli, black pepper — 5 g
instructions: Mix flaked boiled fish with onion, ginger, green chilli and black pepper.
Shape into a flat cutlet.
Pan-fry in oil until golden and firm on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Toast the bread and sandwich the cutlet inside.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Second fish-based recipe in the database, giving non-vegetarian users a real choice beyond chicken and egg
Cutlet-sandwich format is portable, unlike the curry-rice fish preparation
Kerala-style seasoning gives a distinct regional flavour

name: ZITLAS Fenugreek Seed Paneer Chilla
description: A besan chilla batter infused with soaked, ground fenugreek (methi) seeds and paneer — using the seed rather than the leaf, for a distinctly bitter-edged, mineral-rich flavour.
ingredients: Fenugreek seeds, soaked and ground — 5 g
instructions: Soak fenugreek seeds in water for at least 4 hours, then grind to a paste.
Whisk besan with water, the fenugreek paste and turmeric into a smooth batter.
Mix in crumbled paneer.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a round.
Cook until golden on both sides with a little oil, and serve.
why_it_works: Using fenugreek seeds (not leaves) gives a genuinely different, more medicinal flavour profile from the Methi Paneer Paratha elsewhere in the database
Fenugreek seeds are traditionally used for blood sugar support in Indian home remedies
Distinct enough in both ingredient and preparation to stand apart from other chillas

name: ZITLAS Moong Dal Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with whole cooked moong dal, thickened and spiced — a distinct pulse filling from sattu, rajma or soya-based stuffed parathas.
ingredients: Moong dal, cooked and thickened — 90 g
Cumin powder, ginger, green chilli — 5 g
instructions: Cook moong dal with minimal water until soft, then continue cooking uncovered to dry it out into a thick, moist filling; season with cumin, ginger and green chilli.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the dal mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Whole-dal filling gives a chunkier texture than the smoother sattu or besan-based stuffed parathas
Different legume filling from the Rajma Paratha or Soya Keema Paratha elsewhere
Traditional dal paratha technique, genuinely fitness-relevant due to its protein and fiber load

name: ZITLAS Buckwheat Vegetable Chilla
description: A savoury buckwheat (kuttu) flour chilla loaded with vegetables — distinct from the plain fasting-style Kuttu Pancake with Curd, treated here as a regular protein-and-fiber breakfast.
instructions: Whisk kuttu flour with water into a thick, spreadable batter.
Mix in grated carrot, onion, cumin seeds and green chilli.
Heat a tawa, pour the batter and spread into a thick round (kuttu doesn't spread thin easily).
Cook 2-3 minutes per side with a little oil until firm and lightly browned.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Vegetable-loaded savoury version gives kuttu a genuinely different everyday use, separate from its plain fasting-day preparation elsewhere in the database
Gluten-free flour choice
Distinct nutty flavour keeps chilla rotation varied

name: ZITLAS Black Chana Ragda Bowl
description: A wet, tangy black chana curry (ragda) eaten as a warm bowl — a distinct wet-curry chaat format from the drier chana sundal or chana chaat toast.
ingredients: Ragda masala or garam masala, tamarind — 5 g
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add tomato and cook until soft.
Add boiled black chana, ragda masala and tamarind with enough water to form a thin, wet gravy.
Simmer 8-10 minutes, mashing a few chana lightly to thicken the gravy naturally.
Serve hot in a bowl, topped with chopped onion if liked.
why_it_works: Deliberately wet, gravy-style consistency is genuinely different from the dry-tossed sundal or the toast-piled chaat elsewhere
Street-food ragda-pattice flavour without the fried pattice
Filling, warming bowl for cooler mornings

name: ZITLAS Paneer Vegetable Kofta Bowl
description: Steamed (not fried) paneer-vegetable kofta balls served in a light tomato gravy bowl — a distinct ball-in-gravy format not used elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Mix grated paneer with grated vegetables and rice flour into a firm dough; shape into small balls.
Steam the balls in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 10 minutes until firm, rather than deep-frying.
Separately, cook tomato with oil and garam masala into a light gravy.
Add the steamed koftas to the gravy just before serving, simmering 2 minutes to warm through.
why_it_works: Steaming instead of deep-frying keeps this meaningfully lighter than a restaurant-style kofta
Ball-and-gravy bowl format is genuinely different from every roll, paratha or bhurji elsewhere
Vegetables are built into the kofta itself, not a side

name: ZITLAS Barley Porridge Bowl
description: A warm porridge made from barley (jau) flour cooked with milk — an uncommon grain choice with a distinct fiber and mineral profile from oats, ragi or rajgira porridges.
instructions: Whisk barley flour into a little cold milk to avoid lumps.
Heat the rest of the milk, add the flour mixture and stir continuously.
Simmer 6-8 minutes until thickened.
Stir in jaggery and cardamom powder, cook 1-2 more minutes, and serve warm.
why_it_works: Barley is a genuinely uncommon breakfast grain in most Indian households, offering different soluble fiber than oats or millets
Same simple porridge technique but a distinctly different base ingredient
Good option for grain variety across the week

name: ZITLAS Soya Chunk Cutlet Sandwich
description: Ground rehydrated soya chunks shaped into pan-fried cutlets and sandwiched in bread — a distinct patty-sandwich format from the loose soya fillings used in rolls or frankies.
ingredients: Soya chunks, rehydrated and ground — 70 g
instructions: Coarsely grind the rehydrated soya chunks and mix with onion, rice flour and garam masala into a firm mixture.
Shape into a flat cutlet.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp and golden on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Toast the bread and sandwich the cutlet inside.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Patty format holds together for a sandwich, unlike the wet sabzi or dry keema-style soya fillings elsewhere
Genuinely different construction technique from the moong dal or rajma-oats tikki sandwiches
Good lunchbox option

name: ZITLAS Paneer and Vegetable Momos
description: Steamed North-East-Indian-style dumplings filled with grated paneer and finely chopped vegetables — a steamed dumpling format entirely distinct from any roll, roti or rice dish in the database.
instructions: Knead maida with water into a smooth, firm dough; rest 15 minutes.
Mix grated paneer with cabbage, carrot, ginger, garlic and soy sauce for the filling.
Roll small discs of dough, place a spoon of filling in the centre and pleat closed into a momo shape.
Steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle), using a steamer plate, for 10-12 minutes.
Serve hot with a spicy chilli dip.
why_it_works: Steamed dumpling format is genuinely unlike anything else in the database — no roti, rice or roll base at all
Reflects North-East Indian food culture, broadening the database's regional range
Vegetables and protein both folded inside a single bite-sized unit

name: ZITLAS Mixed Sprouts Dhokla
description: A steamed dhokla made from a blend of ground mixed sprouts rather than a single pulse — a fifth distinct dhokla base in the database, using multiple legumes at once.
instructions: Grind mixed sprouts with curd and a little water into a thick batter; rest 15 minutes.
Add eno fruit salt just before steaming and mix gently.
Pour into a greased tin and steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 12-15 minutes.
Cool slightly, cut into squares, and temper mustard and sesame seeds in oil poured over the top.
why_it_works: Using a blend of sprouted legumes rather than one single pulse gives a broader amino acid profile than any single-pulse dhokla in the database
Distinct texture from the smoother besan or moong dal versions
Steamed, low added fat

name: ZITLAS Corn Cheela
description: A besan chilla batter with coarsely crushed corn kernels mixed in — a distinct texture and natural sweetness from any other chilla in the database.
ingredients: Boiled corn kernels, coarsely crushed — 50 g
instructions: Whisk besan with water into a smooth batter, then mix in crushed corn, cumin seeds and green chilli.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a round.
Cook until golden on both sides with a little oil.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Corn adds natural sweetness and a distinct pop of texture not present in any other besan-based chilla here
Kid-friendly flavour, good for a family breakfast rotation
Simple, one-pan, quick preparation

name: ZITLAS Roasted Makhana Chaat Bowl
description: Roasted makhana tossed warm with chopped vegetables and chaat masala — a savoury chaat-style bowl distinct from the yogurt parfait or dry trail-mix uses of makhana elsewhere.
instructions: Dry-roast the makhana in a little oil until crisp, about 4-5 minutes.
Toss the warm roasted makhana with onion, tomato, chaat masala and a squeeze of lemon.
Serve immediately while the makhana is still crisp.
why_it_works: Third distinct makhana format in the database (yogurt parfait, dry trail mix, now a warm savoury chaat), each genuinely different in preparation and eating experience
Very low calorie, high volume
Quick and needs almost no cleanup

name: ZITLAS Soya Granule Idli
description: Regular idli batter enriched with finely ground soya granules mixed in before steaming — a third distinct protein-boosted idli approach alongside the paneer-stuffed and rava versions elsewhere.
instructions: Mix the finely ground soya granules into the fermented idli batter just before steaming, stirring gently to keep the batter airy.
Pour into greased idli moulds and steam for 10-12 minutes until a knife comes out clean.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in a little oil and drizzle over before serving.
why_it_works: Soya granules blend into the batter itself, giving an even protein distribution rather than a pocket of filling
Distinct from both the paneer-stuffed idli and the vegetable rava idli in construction and protein source
Still fully steamed, no added fat beyond the tempering

name: ZITLAS Multigrain Paratha with Peanut Chutney
description: A paratha made from a multigrain flour blend (not single-grain bajra or wheat), paired specifically with a peanut chutney — different grain base and pairing from the Bajra Roti with Peanut Chutney.
instructions: Knead the multigrain flour into a dough with water; roll out into a paratha.
Roast on a hot tawa with a little oil until golden with brown spots on both sides.
For the chutney, dry-roast peanuts and pound coarsely with garlic, red chilli and salt.
Serve the paratha hot with the peanut chutney.
why_it_works: Multigrain blend (several grains at once) gives a broader fiber and mineral profile than the single-grain Bajra Roti elsewhere
Paratha (with fat worked into layers) is a different texture from a flat roti even with a similar pairing
Same reliable peanut-chutney protein pairing, different grain base

name: ZITLAS Vermicelli Egg Upma
description: Roasted vermicelli upma with scrambled egg folded through — using egg rather than soya as the protein addition, distinct from the Soya Vermicelli Upma in Batch 2.
instructions: Dry-roast the vermicelli until light golden; set aside.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then saute onion and carrot for 3 minutes.
Push the vegetables to one side, crack in the egg and scramble it in the empty space.
Add the roasted vermicelli with hot water (roughly equal volume), mix everything together, and cook covered until the water is absorbed.
why_it_works: Egg-based protein addition gives a genuinely different flavour and texture from the soya-chunk version already in the database
Still cooks in one pan in under 20 minutes
Good option for egg-eating users who don't want soya

name: ZITLAS Paneer Sprouts Salad Bowl
description: A cold, no-cook salad combining cubed paneer with mixed sprouts — distinct from the cooked Sprout Paneer Tikki, this stays entirely raw and dressed simply.
instructions: Toss cubed paneer with mixed sprouts and chopped cucumber.
Dress with lemon juice, black pepper and chaat masala.
Mix gently and eat immediately for the best texture.
why_it_works: Fully raw, no-cook format is a genuinely different way to eat paneer and sprouts together from the cooked tikki version elsewhere
Two protein sources combined with zero cooking
Very quick assembly, good for a rushed morning

name: ZITLAS Jowar Roti with Peanut Curry
description: A sorghum (jowar) flatbread served with a light peanut-based curry — a new grain base paired with a curry rather than a dry chutney.
instructions: Knead jowar flour with warm water (it needs warm water to bind) and pat into a flatbread; cook on a hot tawa.
For the curry, heat oil, temper cumin, add tomato and cook soft, then stir in ground peanuts with water to form a light curry.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Serve the roti hot with the peanut curry.
why_it_works: Jowar is a distinct gluten-free grain from bajra or ragi already in the database
Curry format (not dry chutney) changes how the peanuts are eaten
Naturally gluten-free

name: ZITLAS Foxtail Millet Pongal
description: A South Indian pongal made with foxtail millet and moong dal, tempered with ghee, pepper and cumin — a distinct one-pot format from any upma or khichdi.
ingredients: Black pepper, cumin seeds, ginger — 4 g
instructions: Dry-roast moong dal lightly, then pressure cook with foxtail millet and water (1:4 ratio) for 3 whistles until soft and porridge-like.
Heat ghee, temper crushed black pepper, cumin seeds and chopped ginger.
Pour the tempering over the cooked pongal and mix.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Pongal's soft, tempered rice-porridge technique is genuinely different from khichdi or upma preparation
Foxtail millet swap keeps the traditional method but changes the grain profile
Traditional South Indian temple food reframed as a fitness breakfast

name: ZITLAS Lobia Salad Bowl
description: A no-cook salad of boiled black-eyed peas (lobia) with onion, tomato and lemon — introducing a legume not used elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Toss boiled lobia with onion and tomato.
Add lemon juice and chaat masala.
Mix well and eat immediately.
why_it_works: Lobia is a genuinely new legume for the database, broadening protein-source diversity as required
Entirely no-cook
High fiber, low cost

name: ZITLAS Whole Green Gram Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with whole cooked green gram (moong, not split) — a chunkier, whole-legume filling distinct from the split-dal Moong Dal Paratha.
ingredients: Whole green gram, boiled and mashed — 90 g
Cumin powder, ginger, green chilli — 5 g
instructions: Boil whole green gram until soft, drain well and mash coarsely with cumin powder, ginger and green chilli.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the filling and seal.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Whole-bean texture is noticeably different from the smoother split-dal paratha already in the database
Uses the whole legume including its skin, adding extra fiber
Different pulse-paratha option from sattu, rajma or soya

name: ZITLAS Curd Rice with Pomegranate
description: Classic curd rice finished with fresh pomegranate seeds instead of the usual peanut tempering — a distinct sweet-tart variation.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, oil — 4 ml
instructions: Mash the cold rice slightly and mix with curd.
Quickly temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in a few drops of oil and stir in.
Top generously with fresh pomegranate seeds just before serving.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
why_it_works: Pomegranate adds a fresh, antioxidant-rich topping genuinely different from the peanut version already in the database
Almost entirely no-cook
Visually distinct and appealing for repeat use

name: ZITLAS Ragi Idli
description: Steamed idli made from a ragi-flour-enriched batter — a fourth distinct grain base for idli in the database, after rava, soya granule and paneer-stuffed.
instructions: Mix ragi flour into the fermented idli batter, adding a little water to keep it pourable.
Rest 10 minutes.
Pour into greased idli moulds and steam for 10-12 minutes in a pressure cooker without the whistle.
Serve hot with chutney or sambar.
why_it_works: Ragi adds calcium and fiber not present in a plain rice-urad idli
Distinct from the other three idli variants already in the database by using ragi specifically
Still fully steamed, no added fat

name: ZITLAS Horse Gram (Kulith) Usal Bowl
description: A Maharashtrian-style usal made from sprouted horse gram (kulith) — an iron-rich legume distinct from moong, chana or matki already used in the database's usal recipes.
ingredients: Horse gram, sprouted and boiled — 120 g
Goda masala or garam masala — 4 g
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add tomato and cook soft.
Add boiled horse gram and goda masala with a little water; simmer 6-8 minutes.
Serve hot as a bowl, with lemon if liked.
why_it_works: Horse gram is notably higher in iron than the other legumes already used for usal in the database
Traditionally considered warming and used in winter cooking
One-pan, genuinely regional

name: ZITLAS Peanut Chutney Idli Bowl
description: Plain steamed idli broken into a bowl and tossed with peanut chutney and a warm tempering — a deconstructed idli format distinct from serving idli whole with a side.
instructions: Steam idlis as usual and let cool slightly.
Grind peanuts with garlic, red chilli and a little water into a thick chutney.
Break the idlis into bite-sized pieces into a bowl.
Toss with the peanut chutney and a mustard-seed tempering in hot oil.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Broken-and-tossed format is a genuinely different eating experience from whole idli with a side dip
Peanut chutney coats every piece rather than being used for dipping
Repurposes the same idli technique in a distinct way

name: ZITLAS Masoor Dal Cheela
description: A savoury crepe made from ground red lentil (masoor dal) batter — a different pulse base from moong, chana or besan cheelas.
ingredients: Masoor dal, soaked and ground — 60 g
instructions: Grind soaked masoor dal with a little water into a smooth batter.
Mix in onion, cumin seeds and green chilli.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread thin.
Cook until golden on both sides with a little oil.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Masoor dal is a distinct pulse from moong, chana or besan already used for cheelas in the database
Cooks quickly since masoor dal doesn't need long soaking
Mild flavour, easy to season either way

name: ZITLAS Air-Fried Urad Dal Vada Bowl
description: Urad dal vadas air-fried and served dry with chutney rather than soaked in curd — a distinct bowl format from the Air-Fried Moong Dahi Vada.
ingredients: Urad dal, soaked and ground — 100 g
instructions: Grind soaked urad dal with ginger and green chilli into a thick, fluffy batter (whip well for airiness).
Shape into small discs with a hole in the centre and brush with oil.
Air fry at 180°C for 12-15 minutes, flipping once, until golden.
Serve dry with coconut chutney on the side, not soaked in curd.
why_it_works: Dry-with-chutney serving is a genuinely different eating experience from the curd-soaked moong version already in the database
Air frying keeps this far lower in fat than a traditional deep-fried vada
Classic South Indian breakfast made lighter

name: ZITLAS Little Millet Upma
description: Upma made with little millet (kutki) instead of rava — a different, less common millet from the foxtail or bajra versions already in the database.
instructions: Rinse the little millet and soak for 15 minutes.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, roast peanuts, then saute vegetables 3 minutes.
Add the soaked millet and water in a 1:2.5 ratio, cover and simmer 12-15 minutes until soft.
Fluff and serve hot.
why_it_works: Little millet is a genuinely uncommon grain outside dedicated millet cooking, broadening grain diversity as required
Lower glycemic impact than rava
Same familiar upma technique, different base grain

name: ZITLAS Brown Chana Chaat Wrap
description: A tangy brown chana chaat wrapped inside a roti — combining a no-cook chaat filling with a cooked wrap base, distinct from the chana chaat toast.
instructions: Roll out and roast the atta into a roti; keep warm.
Toss boiled brown chana with onion, lemon juice and chaat masala.
Spoon the chana chaat onto the warm roti and roll tightly.
Serve immediately.
why_it_works: Wrap format is a genuinely different way to eat chana chaat from piling it on toast
Portable for a commute unlike the open toast version
Brown chana has a nuttier flavour than white chana

name: ZITLAS Sprouted Moth Bean Cutlet
description: Sprouted matki (moth bean) mashed and shaped into pan-fried cutlets — a distinct patty format from the wet Matki Usal Bowl already in the database.
ingredients: Sprouted matki, boiled and mashed — 100 g
instructions: Mash boiled matki with onion, rice flour and spices until it holds together.
Shape into small flat cutlets.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp and golden on both sides.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Patty format, unlike the wet usal bowl already using the same legume, gives a genuinely different eating experience
Crisp exterior contrasts with the soft usal version
Good lunchbox-style option

name: ZITLAS Jowar Bhakri with Curd and Peanuts
description: A thick, hand-patted jowar bhakri (not rolled like a roti) served with curd and roasted peanuts — a distinct bread-making technique from the thinner Jowar Roti earlier in this batch.
instructions: Knead jowar flour with warm water and pat out by hand into a thick round (bhakri is patted, not rolled with a pin).
Cook on a hot tawa until browned on both sides, brushing with a little ghee.
Serve with a side of curd and roasted peanuts.
why_it_works: Hand-patted bhakri technique produces a thicker, denser bread than a rolled roti, genuinely different eating experience
Traditional Maharashtrian rural breakfast combination
Curd and peanuts on the side supply protein the grain lacks

name: ZITLAS Mixed Vegetable Cutlet Sandwich
description: A pan-fried mixed vegetable cutlet (potato, peas, carrot) sandwiched in toasted bread — a paneer-free, protein-light option balanced by the bread's own protein.
instructions: Mash boiled potato with peas, coriander and green chilli into a firm mixture.
Shape into a flat cutlet.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp and golden on both sides.
Toast the bread and sandwich the cutlet inside.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Deliberately paneer-free option per the diversity requirement to not over-rely on paneer for vegetarian recipes
Classic Indian cutlet-sandwich comfort food
Works well as an occasional lower-protein, higher-carb breakfast for variety

name: ZITLAS Palak Besan Chilla
description: A besan chilla batter with a large proportion of blended spinach (palak) mixed in — distinct from a plain besan chilla by making spinach the dominant flavour, not a small addition.
instructions: Blend spinach with a little water into a smooth puree.
Whisk besan with the spinach puree, cumin seeds and ajwain into a batter.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a round.
Cook until golden on both sides with a little oil.
Serve with curd.
why_it_works: Spinach is blended in as the primary liquid, not a minor mix-in, making this genuinely different from a plain chilla with a few chopped greens
Distinct green colour and iron content
Naturally vegan

name: ZITLAS Chana Dal Vegetable Pulao
description: A rice pulao cooked with chana dal (not whole chana) and vegetables — a dal-in-pulao format distinct from the Chana Pulao Bowl, which used boiled whole chana.
instructions: Soak chana dal for 20 minutes.
Heat oil, temper whole spices, saute vegetables 3 minutes, then add rice, soaked chana dal and garam masala.
Add water in the standard ratio and pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Fluff and serve hot.
why_it_works: Chana dal (split, quicker-cooking) gives a different texture and cooking time from whole chana used in the earlier Chana Pulao Bowl
One-pot, vegetable-forward preparation
Good family-portion breakfast

name: ZITLAS Peanut Sprouts Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with crushed peanuts and moong sprouts together — a crunchy, textured filling distinct from any smooth dal or paneer stuffing.
instructions: Mix chopped moong sprouts with crushed peanuts, green chilli and coriander for the filling.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Crunchy sprout-and-peanut texture is genuinely different from every smooth-filling paratha in the database
Two protein sources combined directly in the stuffing
Distinct bite from any dal-based filling

name: ZITLAS Boiled Egg Chaat Bowl
description: Boiled egg tossed chaat-style with onion, tomato and tangy chutney — distinct from the sprouts-and-lemon Boiled Egg Sprouts Bowl by using a chaat masala and chutney profile instead.
instructions: Chop the boiled eggs into quarters.
Toss with onion, tomato, a spoon of green chutney and chaat masala.
Mix gently and serve immediately.
why_it_works: Chutney-and-chaat-masala flavour profile is distinctly different from the lemon-and-pepper Boiled Egg Sprouts Bowl already in the database
No sprouts, so a genuinely different texture and ingredient set
Entirely no-cook

name: ZITLAS Little Millet Idli
description: Steamed idli made with little millet blended into the batter — a fifth distinct grain base for idli in the database.
ingredients: Little millet, soaked and ground — 100 g
instructions: Soak little millet for 4-6 hours, then grind into a smooth batter and mix with the fermented urad dal batter and curd.
Rest 15 minutes.
Pour into greased idli moulds and steam for 10-12 minutes.
Serve hot with chutney.
why_it_works: Little millet is a genuinely uncommon idli base, giving different fiber and mineral content from rice-based idli
Fifth distinct idli variant in the database, each using a different primary grain or protein strategy
Fully steamed

name: ZITLAS Kodo Millet Khichdi
description: A khichdi made with kodo millet instead of rice — a genuinely different grain base from the bajra khichdi or masala oats khichdi already in the database.
instructions: Rinse kodo millet and moong dal together.
Heat oil, temper cumin seeds, saute vegetables 2-3 minutes, then add the millet-dal mix and turmeric.
Add water (roughly 1:3) and pressure cook for 3 whistles until soft.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Kodo millet is a genuinely uncommon grain outside dedicated millet households, distinct in fiber profile from bajra or oats
Same reliable khichdi technique, different grain base each time keeps the database from feeling repetitive
One-pot, low active effort

name: ZITLAS Peanut Sprouts Dosa
description: A dosa batter enriched with ground peanuts and moong sprouts mixed in — raising both protein and texture, distinct from a plain or ragi dosa.
instructions: Mix ground peanuts and chopped moong sprouts into the fermented dosa batter.
Heat a tawa, pour the batter and spread into a dosa.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until crisp, then flip briefly.
Serve hot with chutney.
why_it_works: Two mix-ins added directly into the batter give a distinctly different texture (slightly gritty, crunchy) from any other dosa in the database
Higher protein than a plain or ragi dosa
Still cooks with the familiar dosa technique

name: ZITLAS Besan Kadhi Bowl
description: A warm, tangy besan-and-curd kadhi eaten as a breakfast bowl — a wet gravy format entirely distinct from any chilla, dhokla or dosa use of besan in the database.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 4 g
instructions: Whisk besan into curd and water until completely smooth with no lumps.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and turmeric.
Pour in the besan-curd mixture and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring often to prevent curdling, for 10-12 minutes until thickened slightly.
Serve warm in a bowl.
why_it_works: Wet, gravy-style kadhi is a genuinely different besan preparation from every chilla or dhokla elsewhere in the database
Curd base makes this notably higher protein than a plain besan dish
Traditionally a lunch dish, reframed here as a light savoury breakfast bowl

name: ZITLAS Multi-Dal Cheela
description: A cheela batter made from three different dals ground together (masoor, moong and urad) — a broader amino-acid-profile cheela distinct from any single-dal version.
instructions: Grind the three soaked dals together with a little water into a smooth batter.
Mix in onion and cumin seeds.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread thin.
Cook until golden on both sides with a little oil.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Combining three pulses at once gives a broader amino acid profile than any single-dal cheela already in the database
Genuinely different flavour from blending three dals rather than using one
Same familiar cheela technique

name: ZITLAS Plain Vegetable Uttapam
description: A basic rice-urad uttapam topped only with vegetables, no protein add-in beyond the batter itself — included specifically to diversify the database with a low-effort, fully traditional option.
instructions: Heat a tawa and pour a thick ladle of batter, spreading only slightly.
Scatter onion and tomato over the top and press gently.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until golden, then flip briefly.
Serve hot with chutney or sambar.
why_it_works: A straightforward traditional option without extra grain or protein mix-ins, useful for users who just want the classic version alongside the enriched variants elsewhere in the database
Fermented batter still provides real protein from the urad dal itself
Simple, fast, familiar

name: ZITLAS Green Peas Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with mashed and spiced green peas (matar) — a seasonal vegetable filling distinct from lauki, beetroot or methi.
ingredients: Green peas, boiled and mashed — 70 g
Ginger, green chilli, garam masala — 5 g
instructions: Mash boiled green peas coarsely with ginger, green chilli and garam masala.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the pea mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Matar (green pea) filling is a distinct seasonal vegetable option from the other stuffed parathas in the database
Naturally sweet filling appeals to a different palate than spiced paneer or dal fillings
Traditional winter-season combination

name: ZITLAS Bengali-Style Egg Curry with Bajra Roti
description: A mustard-oil, panch-phoron-spiced Bengali egg curry served with bajra roti — a distinct regional spice profile and grain pairing from the Egg Curry with Multigrain Roti in Batch 2.
instructions: Knead bajra flour into a dough and pat out into a roti; roast on a tawa.
Heat mustard oil, temper panch phoron, saute onion until golden, add potato and turmeric, cook 5 minutes.
Add water for a light gravy and simmer 5 minutes.
Halve the boiled eggs and add, simmering 2-3 minutes.
Serve hot with the bajra roti.
why_it_works: Panch phoron and mustard oil give a genuinely distinct regional flavour from the garam-masala-based multigrain version already in the database
Bajra roti pairing is different from the multigrain roti used before
Potato addition changes the gravy's texture and heartiness

name: ZITLAS Puffed Rice (Murmura) Bhel Bowl
description: A light, no-cook bhel made from puffed rice, vegetables and tamarind chutney — a genuinely different base ingredient (murmura, not poha) from every other bhel or chaat in the database.
instructions: Combine puffed rice, onion, tomato and peanuts in a bowl.
Add tamarind chutney and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Toss well and eat immediately before the puffed rice softens.
why_it_works: Puffed rice is a genuinely new base ingredient for the database, distinct in texture (light, airy) from poha or semiya used elsewhere
Very low calorie, high volume
Zero cooking, classic Mumbai-street-style bhel at home

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Semiya Upma with Peanuts
description: A fully vegetarian vermicelli upma using peanuts as the only protein add-in — distinct from both the soya and egg vermicelli versions already in the database.
instructions: Dry-roast the vermicelli until light golden; set aside.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, roast peanuts, then saute vegetables 3 minutes.
Add the roasted vermicelli with hot water (roughly equal volume) and cook covered until absorbed.
why_it_works: Peanut-only protein strategy gives users a soya-free, egg-free vermicelli option, completing the set of three distinct protein approaches to the same base dish
Very budget-friendly
Familiar, quick technique

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Peanut Frankie
description: A frankie roll filled with a spiced mixed-vegetable and crushed-peanut filling — a fully vegan frankie option distinct from the soya and paneer versions already in the database.
instructions: Roll out and roast the atta into a roti on a tawa until slightly charred at the edges.
Heat oil, saute vegetables until soft, then mix in crushed peanuts.
Spread chutneys on the roti, add the vegetable-peanut filling, and roll tightly.
Serve immediately.
why_it_works: Completes a set of three protein strategies (soya, paneer, peanut) for the same frankie format, letting users pick by preference or budget
Fully vegan and generally the cheapest of the three frankie options
Same proven charred-roti technique

name: ZITLAS Amaranth Leaves (Chaulai) Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with chopped amaranth leaves (chaulai saag) — a leafy green distinct from spinach or methi already used in the database's parathas.
instructions: Blanch the amaranth leaves briefly, squeeze out excess water and chop finely.
Mix with garlic and red chilli powder for the filling.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the leaves mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Amaranth leaves are a distinct leafy green from spinach or methi already used in the database, adding calcium and iron
Genuinely different regional green vegetable choice
Traditional North Indian saag-paratha style

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Khakhra Chaat
description: Multigrain khakhra broken into pieces and tossed chaat-style with curd, chutney and vegetables — distinct from simply spreading peanut butter on whole khakhras.
instructions: Break the khakhra into bite-sized pieces into a bowl.
Add curd, onion, tomato, chaat masala and a spoon of green chutney.
Toss gently and eat immediately, while the khakhra still has some crunch.
why_it_works: Deconstructed chaat format is a genuinely different way to eat khakhra from the simple spread-and-stack version already in the database
Curd adds meaningfully more protein than the peanut butter version
No cooking involved

name: ZITLAS Cowpea (Chawli) Sabzi Roti Roll
description: A wet, spiced cowpea (chawli/lobia) sabzi rolled inside a roti — a cooked-curry roll format distinct from the raw Lobia Salad Bowl earlier in this batch.
instructions: Roll out and roast the atta into rotis; keep warm.
Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cook until soft.
Add boiled chawli and garam masala with a splash of water, simmer 8-10 minutes into a slightly wet sabzi.
Spoon onto a roti and roll, letting some gravy soak in.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Cooked, gravy-style preparation gives cowpea a genuinely different role from the raw salad version earlier in this batch
Same legume, two legitimately distinct cooking techniques and eating experiences
Homely, filling breakfast

name: ZITLAS Air-Fried Sabudana Vada
description: Sabudana shaped into vadas and air-fried instead of the more common khichdi preparation — a distinct format from the Sabudana Peanut Khichdi already in the database.
instructions: Mix soaked sabudana with mashed potato, crushed peanuts, green chilli and cumin seeds.
Shape into small discs and brush with oil.
Air fry at 190°C for 12-15 minutes, flipping once, until golden and crisp.
Serve with curd or chutney.
Note: sabudana needs overnight soaking, not counted in active prep time above.
why_it_works: Vada (patty) format eaten with chutney is genuinely different from the soft, spoonable khichdi version already in the database
Air frying keeps this far lower in fat than the traditional deep-fried version
Same fasting-day ingredient, different construction and cooking method

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Semolina Cutlet
description: A pan-fried cutlet made from cooked rava (semolina) mixed with vegetables — a solid cutlet format distinct from rava idli or rava upma.
instructions: Cook rava with water and finely chopped vegetables into a thick, dry mixture; cool completely (this is essential for shaping).
Shape into small flat cutlets.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp and golden on both sides.
Serve with ketchup or chutney.
why_it_works: Solid cutlet format is a genuinely different use of rava from the soft idli or loose upma preparations already in the database
Good make-ahead option since the rava mixture needs to cool before shaping anyway
Kid-friendly, familiar comfort food

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Idiyappam Bowl
description: Steamed rice-flour string hoppers (idiyappam) tossed with a light vegetable stir-fry — a distinct noodle-like format not used anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Knead rice flour with boiling water into a smooth, pliable dough.
Press through an idiyappam press (or a fine sieve) directly into a steamer plate to form noodle strands, and steam for 8-10 minutes.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, saute vegetables 3-4 minutes.
Gently toss the steamed idiyappam strands with the vegetables.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: String-hopper texture is entirely unlike any dosa, idli or roti already in the database
Steamed, essentially fat-free base
Kerala/Tamil Nadu home-style breakfast rarely represented in fitness recipe collections

name: ZITLAS Egg Idiyappam Bowl
description: Steamed idiyappam string hoppers tossed with scrambled egg — a protein-added variant of the Vegetable Idiyappam Bowl, using the same steaming technique.
instructions: Knead rice flour with boiling water into a smooth dough and press into idiyappam strands; steam for 8-10 minutes.
Heat oil, saute onion, then scramble in the beaten egg until just cooked.
Gently toss the steamed idiyappam strands with the scrambled egg.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Egg addition raises the protein of the same idiyappam base meaningfully above the vegetable-only version
Distinct from every other egg preparation in the database by the noodle-like idiyappam texture
Same steaming technique, different finishing

name: ZITLAS Air-Fried Chana Dal Vada
description: Chana dal ground and shaped into vadas, air-fried and served dry — a distinct dal and format from the urad dal vada bowl earlier in this batch.
ingredients: Chana dal, soaked and coarsely ground — 100 g
instructions: Coarsely grind soaked chana dal (keep it chunky, not smooth) with green chilli.
Mix in onion and fennel seeds.
Shape into small discs and brush with oil.
Air fry at 180°C for 12-15 minutes, flipping once, until golden.
Serve with coconut or mint chutney.
why_it_works: Chana dal gives a chunkier, nuttier vada than the smooth urad dal version, a genuinely different texture
Fennel seed seasoning is a distinct flavour choice from the ginger-based urad version
Air fried, far lower fat than deep frying

name: ZITLAS Roasted Soybean Trail Mix Bowl
description: Whole roasted soybeans mixed with raisins — a dry, portable bowl using whole soybeans, distinct from the soya chunks, granules or flour used elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Combine roasted whole soybeans and raisins in a small container.
Mix well.
Carry and eat on the move, or as a sit-down bowl.
why_it_works: Whole roasted soybeans have a different fat and fiber profile from the defatted soya chunks or granules used in every other soya recipe here
Entirely dry and shelf-stable, no refrigeration needed
Genuinely no prep beyond mixing

name: ZITLAS Rajma Poha Cutlet Sandwich
description: Leftover rajma bound with crushed poha instead of oats, shaped into cutlets and sandwiched — a distinct binder choice from the Rajma Oats Tikki Sandwich already in the database.
instructions: Mash leftover rajma with crushed poha and chilli powder — the poha absorbs moisture and binds the mixture.
Shape into a flat cutlet.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp on both sides.
Toast the bread and sandwich the cutlet inside.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Poha as a binder gives a noticeably different texture (softer, slightly sticky) from the oats-bound version already in the database
Third genuinely different way to use leftover rajma across the database (paratha, oats tikki, and now poha cutlet)
Good use of two leftovers at once if the poha is also left over

name: ZITLAS Boiled Peanut Chaat Bowl
description: Peanuts boiled (not roasted) and tossed chaat-style — a South Indian coastal technique giving a softer, different texture from every roasted-peanut use in the database.
ingredients: Raw peanuts, boiled in shell and shelled — 80 g
instructions: Pressure cook raw peanuts in their shells with water and a little salt for 3-4 whistles until soft; cool and shell them.
Toss the boiled peanuts with onion, tomato, lemon juice and chaat masala.
Serve at room temperature.
why_it_works: Boiling peanuts gives a completely different, softer texture from every roasted-peanut preparation elsewhere in the database
A genuinely different technique, not just a renamed roasted-peanut chaat
Coastal South Indian street-food style

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Kanji Drink
description: A traditional fermented, mildly spiced vegetable drink (kanji) made with mustard and beetroot — a fermented probiotic drink format used nowhere else in the database.
ingredients: Black salt, red chilli powder — 4 g
instructions: Combine sliced beetroot, water, ground mustard, black salt and chilli powder in a glass jar.
Cover and leave to ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days, stirring once daily.
Once mildly sour and tangy, strain and refrigerate.
Serve chilled, a small glass at a time.
Note: fermentation takes 2-3 days; active prep time above covers assembly only.
why_it_works: A genuinely fermented, probiotic drink — a category not represented anywhere else in the database
Traditional North Indian winter health drink, distinct from any smoothie or lassi
Very low calorie

name: ZITLAS Roasted Chana Dal and Curd Bowl
description: A simple no-cook combination of roasted chana dal (dalia) and curd — a distinct dry-plus-dairy pairing from the buttermilk-and-dry-chana combo already in the database.
ingredients: Roasted cumin powder, black salt — 2 g
instructions: Spoon curd into a bowl.
Mix in roasted chana dal.
Season with roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Eat immediately while the dal is still crunchy.
why_it_works: Curd-based pairing is a distinctly different texture from the liquid buttermilk-and-dry-chana combo already in the database
Two protein sources, genuinely no-cook
Extremely simple for a very rushed morning

name: ZITLAS Sweet Potato Chaat Bowl
description: Boiled sweet potato cubes tossed chaat-style with chutney and spices — a cold, no-cook chaat format distinct from the oven-baked, curd-topped Baked Sweet Potato with Curd.
ingredients: Sweet potato, boiled and cubed — 150 g
instructions: Toss boiled sweet potato cubes with crushed peanuts.
Add lemon juice and chaat masala.
Top with coriander and serve at room temperature.
why_it_works: Cold chaat format is genuinely different from the oven-baked, curd-topped preparation already in the database
Entirely no-cook once the sweet potato is pre-boiled
Naturally sweet-tangy flavour balance

name: ZITLAS Multigrain Khakhra Sandwich
description: Multigrain khakhra used as the bread for a sandwich filled with vegetables and peanut chutney — a sandwich construction distinct from the spread-and-stack or chaat-bowl uses of khakhra elsewhere.
instructions: Spread peanut chutney on one khakhra.
Layer cucumber and tomato slices on top.
Close with a second khakhra to form a sandwich.
Eat immediately, pressing gently to hold together.
why_it_works: Using khakhra as bread rather than a base for spreading or a chaat bowl is a genuinely different construction from the other two khakhra recipes in the database
Entirely no-cook, shelf-stable ingredients
Crisp, portable format

name: ZITLAS Lauki Chilla
description: A besan chilla batter with grated bottle gourd (lauki) mixed in — a chilla format distinct from the Lauki Paratha, using a different cooking technique for the same vegetable.
instructions: Whisk besan with water, cumin seeds and ajwain into a batter.
Mix in grated lauki (no need to squeeze — the batter absorbs the moisture).
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread thin.
Cook until golden on both sides with a little oil.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Chilla technique (thin, pan-cooked) is genuinely different from the stuffed-paratha use of the same vegetable already in the database

Quick, one-pan preparation

name: ZITLAS Roasted Chana and Puffed Rice Chivda
description: A dry roasted mix of chana dal, puffed rice and peanuts tossed with light spices — a snack-style chivda distinct from the roti-based Leftover Roti Chivda.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, roast peanuts and roasted chana dal briefly.
Add turmeric and puffed rice, tossing on low heat for 3-4 minutes until well coated and slightly crisp.
Cool slightly and store, or eat warm.
why_it_works: Puffed-rice-based chivda is a genuinely different base from the leftover-roti version already in the database
Can be made in a batch and kept for a few days, unlike most other recipes here
Very low cost per serving

name: ZITLAS Multi-Millet Idli
description: Steamed idli made from a blend of ragi, foxtail and little millet flours together — a sixth idli variant, distinct by combining three millets at once rather than using a single grain.

Rest 15 minutes.
Pour into greased idli moulds and steam for 10-12 minutes.
Serve hot with chutney or sambar.
why_it_works: Combining three different millets gives a broader fiber and mineral spread than any single-millet idli already in the database
Distinct from the single-grain ragi or little millet idli variants by using all three at once
Fully steamed

name: ZITLAS Boiled Chana and Peanut Salad
description: A no-cook salad combining boiled white chana with roasted peanuts — a distinct pairing bowl from the Sprout Peanut Salad Cup, which used sprouts rather than boiled chana.

Add lemon juice and chaat masala.
Mix well and eat immediately.
why_it_works: Boiled chana (softer texture) rather than raw sprouts gives a genuinely different bite from the earlier sprout-peanut salad in the database
Two protein sources, entirely no-cook
Simple, cheap, quick

name: ZITLAS Curd Sprouts Bowl
description: A simple no-cook bowl of mixed sprouts folded into curd — using dairy rather than paneer as the pairing protein, distinct from the Paneer Sprouts Salad Bowl.
ingredients: Roasted cumin powder, black salt — 2 g
instructions: Rinse and drain the sprouts well.
Fold into curd.
Season with roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Eat immediately.
why_it_works: Uses curd rather than paneer as the pairing protein, deliberately diversifying away from paneer per the ingredient-diversity requirement
Entirely no-cook
Very simple, cooling combination

name: ZITLAS Oats Waffle with Peanut Butter
description: A crisp waffle made from an oats-egg batter, topped with peanut butter — a waffle format not used anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Blend ground oats, egg and milk into a smooth batter.
Cook on a hot, lightly greased tawa in a thick round, pressing lightly for a waffle-like crisp edge, 2-3 minutes per side.
Top with peanut butter and serve.
why_it_works: Waffle-style crisp texture is genuinely new to the database
No refined flour or added sugar
Quick, one-pan

name: ZITLAS Moong Dal Waffle
description: A savoury vegan waffle made from ground moong dal batter — distinct base and flavour from the sweet oats-egg waffle.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 70 g
instructions: Grind soaked moong dal into a thick batter with onion, cumin seeds and green chilli.
Cook on a hot tawa in a thick round, pressing for crisp edges, 3 minutes per side with a little oil.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Savoury, dal-based waffle format distinct from the sweet version
Fully vegan, high protein

name: ZITLAS Chicken Tikka Wrap
description: Curd-marinated grilled chicken chunks rolled inside a roti — a non-vegetarian tikka format paralleling the Paneer Tikka Skewers but in wrap form.

Roll out and roast a roti.
Fill with the tikka chicken and roll tightly. Serve warm.
why_it_works: Wrap format is different from the skewer presentation of a similar marinade elsewhere
Lean chicken breast keeps fat moderate
Portable for a commute

name: ZITLAS Egg Muffin Breakfast Sandwich
description: A fried egg and toasted bread stacked into a fast-food-style breakfast sandwich — a distinct stacked construction from the toastie or bhurji sandwiches.

Toast two bread slices.
Stack the fried egg between the toasted bread.
Serve immediately while the yolk is warm.
why_it_works: Stacked, fried-egg sandwich is genuinely different from the whisked-omelette toastie already in the database
Extremely fast
Familiar fast-food-inspired format

name: ZITLAS Aloo Methi Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha with a mashed potato and fresh fenugreek leaf filling — a distinct vegetable-leaf pairing from any other paratha in the database.

Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the mixture and seal.
Roll out and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Potato-and-methi combination is a distinct filling pairing from any single-ingredient paratha in the database
Classic North Indian winter combination
Filling, comfort-food breakfast

name: ZITLAS Rajma Galouti Kebab
description: Mashed, spiced rajma shaped into soft, pan-seared kebab patties — a kebab format and finer mash distinct from the chunkier Rajma Chaat or Poha Cutlet.
instructions: Blend boiled rajma into a very fine, smooth paste with ginger-garlic paste and garam masala (galouti kebabs are prized for their smoothness).
Mix in finely chopped onion.
Shape into small flat kebabs.
Pan-sear in oil until browned on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Fine-blended, melt-in-mouth kebab texture is distinctly different from the chunky cutlet or raw chaat uses of rajma elsewhere
Restaurant-style Lucknowi kebab technique made vegetarian
Fourth genuinely different rajma preparation in the database

name: ZITLAS Soya Seekh Kebab
description: Minced, spiced soya granules shaped onto skewers and pan-seared — a skewered kebab format distinct from the tikka-cube or loose-filling soya recipes elsewhere.
ingredients: Soya granules, rehydrated and ground — 80 g
instructions: Grind rehydrated soya granules coarsely and mix with onion, besan, garam masala and ginger-garlic paste into a firm dough.
Mould onto skewers (or shape into logs) into a seekh shape.
Pan-sear, turning frequently, until browned all over, about 8-10 minutes.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Skewered log shape is a distinct format from the loose keema or wet sabzi soya preparations already in the database
Besan acts as a binder, a technique not used for soya elsewhere
Restaurant-style kebab made from an inexpensive protein

name: ZITLAS Chicken Seekh Kebab Roll
description: Minced chicken seekh kebab rolled inside a roti — a distinct non-vegetarian kebab-roll format from the tikka wrap.

Pan-sear, turning frequently, until fully cooked through, about 10-12 minutes.
Roll out and roast a roti.
Wrap the kebabs in the roti and serve warm.
why_it_works: Minced-and-shaped seekh technique is distinct from the cubed-and-marinated tikka technique already in the database
High protein, lean
Portable roll format

name: ZITLAS Egg Kejriwal Toast
description: A Mumbai-club-style fried egg on buttered toast topped with green chilli and coriander — an iconic distinct preparation from any other egg-on-toast recipe here.
instructions: Toast the bread lightly.
Whisk the egg with onion, green chilli and coriander, then cook it directly onto the toast in a pan (egg-topped-toast technique) until set.
Flip briefly to lightly toast the underside, then serve.
why_it_works: Iconic Mumbai club sandwich technique — egg cooked directly onto bread — is a distinct method from a separately-fried egg placed on toast
Genuinely different construction from the Egg Muffin Sandwich in this same batch
Bombay-style street food made simply

name: ZITLAS Moong Dal Pancake Stack

instructions: Grind soaked moong dal with grated carrot and cumin seeds into a thick batter.
Cook small, thick rounds (about 6-7 cm) on a tawa, 2 minutes per side, until golden.
Stack 3-4 small pancakes.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Small, thick, stacked format is genuinely different from a single large thin cheela or dosa

Same reliable moong dal base, different construction

name: ZITLAS Paneer Do Pyaza Toast
description: Paneer cooked with a double portion of onion (do pyaza style) and spread on toast — a distinct onion-forward spice profile from any other paneer toast in the database.

Add paneer cubes, turmeric and coriander powder, cooking 2-3 minutes.
Toast the bread and spoon the paneer do pyaza over the top.
